#
Big news, Peter: our new 2026 election endorsements are officially here!
[](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261023.9XgqhV&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-1245&t=1&akid=1245%2E34582%2EmUb7yY)
Today, I’m proudly endorsing three Democrats running in critical gubernatorial races: Amy Acton in Ohio, David Crowley in Wisconsin, and Cindy Holscher in Kansas.
**[If you’re ready to join me in supporting these three candidates for governor, fund our work in the final 11 days with a grassroots contribution now →](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261023.9XgqhV&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-1245&t=2&akid=1245%2E34582%2EmUb7yY)**
I launched Small Town PAC back in April to put power back into the hands of our neighbors and help Democrats expand the map in small towns and rural communities across the country this November.
Now, in the final stretch of the midterms, we’re adding three more candidates to our Small Town PAC Slate to help them win in three crucial swing states. They are:
**Amy Acton** — a doctor and public health advocate from Youngstown.
**David Crowley** — a lifelong public servant based in Milwaukee.
**Cindy Holscher** — a state senator and former substitute teacher.
Just like our congressional candidates, all three of these leaders know the struggles of small towns and working families _firsthand._
Amy faced abuse and homelessness as a child — she even lived in a tent in the dead of winter. But she worked her way through medical school and dedicated herself to lifting up others, especially children.
David grew up with parents who battled addiction and mental health struggles, never knowing if bills would be paid or food would be on the table. He ran for office and delivered results for Wisconsinites because he learned that when systems fail, families feel it first.
Cindy was raised with Midwestern values on a farm. She’s the daughter of a veteran and an elementary school employee who were able to send her to college and provide a better life thanks to her father’s union construction job and strong public schools.
Each of them knows what it’s like to sit at the kitchen table and wonder how they’re going to cover the electric bill, fill up their gas tank, or budget for their family’s next grocery trip. **Unlike their MAGA opponents, they will fight for the working people of their states and deliver results that make it easier to not just get by in life, but truly thrive.**

A student at UNT recently asked me, “Why are you doing this?”
I think she meant: you're not on the ballot, you're not in office. So what are you still doing out here? I told her the truth – this work makes me feel useful.
It's what keeps me going and keeps me up when otherwise I'd be down. Here's what "this" looks like.
Our volunteers get certified and trained, then head to campuses, coffee shops, and concerts across Texas – meeting young people where they are and personally staying in touch with every one of them to make sure they vote.

Thousands of mail-in ballots are being rejected because of a new law MAGA's state legislature passed to put archaic restrictions on which ballots can be counted. Here is how it works. The ballot now comes with two envelopes: one to seal the ballot in, and a second to put that envelope in. Forget to seal the first envelope, and your ballot gets thrown out. | | == This is an emergency situation. North Carolina has a critical Senate race and a key state Supreme Court race on the ballot this November. And right now, in some of the state's biggest Democratic strongholds, as many as 7-8% of mail-in ballots are being rejected. Last month, Defend Our Courts set aside resources for an emergency GOTV fund in the case that Trump and MAGA tried to rig mail-in voting. We are glad we did, because now we have to scramble to show voters how to properly seal their ballots, and how to request and return a new one if theirs was rejected. But what we set aside will not reach every North Carolina voter we need to. How many we can reach comes down to what we raise in the next 24 hours. Three states are about to decide a lot more than 2026.

| | | |
---
Friend,
---
We've looked at the polling in every swing state and swing race in the country. It's margin of error, either way, almost everywhere.

At this point, it's not about winning anybody over. _It's about who actually shows up._

If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let us explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Here's why... Winning the presidency comes down to 270 electoral votes. Lose Arizona and most of the realistic paths to the White House in 2028 are gone. Lose Nevada and New Hampshire and the Left rebuilds the Blue Wall they lost in 2024.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

## Van Zandt Fire Kills Mother, 4 Children
A [mother and her four children](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL-OszAQxJ_GdEb22uFP4eJr6PK1V6KFXYIlYyLsw8k9_Ym8wrW7mpnfzNd9vKMPPj7-48Yuv5Z9jFxS4Jz5GBfekDh6TuiJlpIilwdmTiMoaKRWEsyIc_YnjxYrcpOiXlfsdNtDezPQ3arVQdc3MAHfDFmrGssA2tLczV3TqqbvK-8uO63AaK00QG0mMsCT1sagxr4TVjH5vB91XjnzC9MS3vvJRz3vWxXcmvMzCfNPwCBgKKXU83SxpusvYPhIBAzXScBAjBTe8sQofzBSluv-nVgu_uBPJy0vHgFDdTh6Fh-CT00rrHps6MMnM_91q9PBbwAAAP__Bml8yQ), the youngest a 3-year-old girl, died after fire ripped through their home near Canton early Wednesday, Van Zandt County Fire Marshal Kevin Palmer said. Three people escaped the mobile home after the fire broke out around 12:30 a.m., but four children were trapped in a bedroom. With trees and a boarded window blocking the way, firefighters [cut through a wall](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LHOozAQBOCnMZ2RvSY_ULi4hu6_9kq0tpdgxZjI3kByT3_iXuHvRhrp02j-fM_fGFPM99-4keX3ss-ZzpqImcq80IaBcqSKMYTlrJnOOzLVGRR8Sa0kmBk9x4PmDptgnQqjbsjqfoT-ZmC4Nau9oep6WkZyLuCgB1RekVNOdc6rTvkm2ovTCozWSgO0xgUD5LQ2BjWOg-gUhch7aXklpjfWJX32g0rr961JdmV-VmF-CZgETOd5to_Ex1UKmC5bwKTVlbWAyUi_xhQKZfmIKVGQIH2JHD2m9JHrq7A8MMu_mANLv78yf-S6vyrJJRYSMDXFhucZU4r1qxedum8Y0_8t_NMPDwv_AgAA__8zfoae) to reach them. Two boys, ages 8 and 5, died at the scene with their sister, while their oldest brother and mother later died at a Dallas hospital. The mother was the daughter of [a county sheriff's deputy](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OHCEQhJ-GyVhBMz9MQOCE7Jw6HDXQ7CKxM6ehvdz56a1ZP4Kj7lJJn6rq18f2gaWW_f4Tn-T4Kx_bTr1VYqZzy_TERHuhhiWl3NtO_Y5MbQMFs9RKgtkwcnnRNuKQXFBp1QM5vaywTAbsNDycoesPaxzzCMkEbYM1iaY5xzSHEIfiLpxWYLRWGuBmQjJAQWtjUONqxagoFT7OGz-I6Qtbrt_Hi85bPJ5DdQ_mzybMDwFegO-933pGvEwBHk8usZIAfzUT4OsRsQrwb5AAT9hYvoXM5SSZkbHKF-7yD-6JZTx-7_wt4zlqWP4dK8CDXSRO4xKiilLbdZVjCJMMKk2SZqQlWhVUVMPp0mcvtZY2L2JU9yeW-g7O_zv4y8HfAAAA__9mAJNy), District Attorney Tonda Curry said. Canton ISD said the children were [students at Canton Elementary](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAQRL-G6miQS8myCxZp1F3alMKaXFqLo8gDuWc5fx8oyB-kHMxgMPN-fawfyJnL8yfu5OWd6lro6JlEqK2JdoxUmDpyjOnohY4nCvUVDFy1NRrcikH4ReuIQ_QPE-92IG_nO8yTg9s0bD7EZCzNt-tkx0ewFOwUx9lRIAppmu4D-7POGnDWGgtwcY_ogB7WOocW7zc1GoostV1kI6E39pR_1xe1S6j7kP0m8tWV-6FgUbAcx3H5JPk8TQXL-UfBkmvArP8Jp8PGOTYqOhJGDbrKRq1rLjo0Fj6zoZbIwrVoTEJNd2nfQb4b6cSNdCFsOmCRWhQsQ_Px6-CcuV9nNZrnjpz_zpP_xfry8CcAAP__Op6QBg) and Canton Intermediate, and counselors will be on both campuses in the coming days. The fire marshal's office hasn't released a cause and says the investigation is ongoing.
## FEMA Denies Aid to Flood Survivors
FEMA denied Gov. Greg Abbott's [request for direct disaster aid](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQxvGnwR0rGGyMCxdp3F3alNbgGXZRsFkBZ1_ePvLlEVKP9Nf8vl8f6wfGFI_nT9x5bl8hrwdfNXFrXNbAOxIfkStGonDVg68nNq4rKLBSKwlmxa3Fk9ceO5q9okl3POtxgnEw4IbuNQdnGVywCjwbNwzUW1JmIu8NedOHLs53TiswWisN8DCeDLDX2hjUODnRK6bYcnm0Fzf-whrSn3xyeWx579L8au1dhfkhYBGwXNf1-H1-8n0UsGBpcUssYLllApaUN0wClu-QDClnkvWznPHMpcp3YiR5y-U_uqRYsTYuEmuNteGx3TEYjeRNTY7Ry0lbK3vXe-mdIjnYfvPocNQ2dGWm9xVTitWOolfPHWP6_rv9797nDH8DAAD__-sdlTU) to households in 30 Texas counties, leaving Hill Country families who lost homes in this summer's flooding without federal help to rebuild. The agency said the damage didn't qualify for household aid, and it also [refused aid for public repairs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0buunEAMBuCngc6ruXA5FBRp6E7alMgz9izW8TIrmIWTPH3E5hHSWfIv__rkX5_zJ4rKev-JDx7Ld8rzyueuXApvc-IHEq_COwpROveVzzsW3mdnXAfWgPMzxiIHzw3WNAZDg615tP3g-ta7j7ZeRhOaELrobUhd6lJDBtE0xhI2fSDb1zJe56xx3lpjnbv5QN5xsNZ7tDh8VI1hkpK3W1m48DfuSX_ng7dbzI9ax6WU5175H5WbKjed53n74nVvr23lJtyKROXKTRetcpPmiFq56eLBPx_ISnIIvVAhac4EKATewLsNYn6t5YolfIhew8L6hC_etkNUGSKWJatEiAtu8o6-DlRi-IMHKgKGkEsBfD753e16D6ltu4CRwHYmQJPaHobWG0g0MAbCofmw9TbS8xRV2bu-asz9gaJvdvnfdx2j-xsAAP__6ISsoA) in eight counties, including Bexar, Atascosa, and Medina. Abbott has until Oct. 28 to appeal. Kerrville officials [said they're disappointed](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0bGSnDAMBuCngU47WIaFLSjS0F3alIxA8p4Sr31jG7h9-wy7eYOUvzTzzejXr4_5g9RruP-kh4zl28U5yJG9lCJpdvIglqCSSZndkYMcdyqSZ2zwCqYBtDOtRXeZW6p5XBq-mVpG09-w7ywOXf05tks_EHYtLTeHN15pkR556JbB9saKrXU8OdOgNaYxiBe7sEVZjLGWDN2Gqm2EtcR0KZ9S5Juy88-4S7qs8VH78bOUr1zZHxVOFU7HcVwOR3QuK5woFV29VDidl1U45ULljC8I_g3fwfkYucLpj6S0q_cCW7pLhiRrDFlZEhWNAc5i4N0MaGDdlTfyQMrwe_PPtwN5S7vuMWV466cKa9xCeQJrplwkvehd0hMoZ82FwiqQZNnUs4Z7hRP2FlznurYbBNqeWmi7_grUyALSkmF2w3VYuU4jfx3qveZrX7XN_UHqXwWV_33sPuLfAAAA__-DU73m), noting families across the city and Kerr County are still struggling to rebuild. The city hopes an appeal will lead FEMA to reconsider and pledged to keep working with local, state, and federal partners to find recovery resources.
## Freed American Lands in San Antonio
A 74-year-old former Michigan teacher held in Russian custody for more than four years [landed in San Antonio](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0b2u4yAQBeCnwd1EMPgnKVxs4-5uu6U1wGCjxRABjm_efpV9hVsf6eh8On--1i8KMaTtNx08t2-f18RXjdwal9XzQY5T4ErBOX_VxNdGjeuKEkdQElCvZFt48dpT52Yj3UN1PKvpgdOg8T50-zxoR17q0WvSTj2QnHa2HzW6UZpRDl2YP3VKolZKKsSbNk4jG6W0JkWPu-glu9ByubWdG39T9fGdX1xuNh9dnPfWnlXoXwIXgct1Xbe_r5M_ocCFSgs2ssDlIxO4xGwpClxq4-fOCfbTGCoOKiWg1HIKGXw-C7yZSoVy1hoogT1ry-4Nhg4LR7B72ChBY7I7FyhsP4PecJWcNn9GcNw4tZCTwAUnDZPzdz_RBMj3CXrZGyBlBtA9j2Z0o7VGdWV2zyvEGOo4iV5uB4X4H9l-es5rxn8BAAD__9CDppg) late Wednesday for care at Brooke Army Medical Center. Stephen Hubbard, who is in poor health, is receiving medical and psychological evaluations before heading home to Michigan. Russia detained him in February 2022, accused him of fighting for Ukraine, and sentenced him to nearly seven years in a penal colony. President Trump said Russia [freed Hubbard at his request](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L3unDAQBPCnMZ0RXvNxFC7S0F3alGiN18fqwCDbnC9vH5FX-HcjjTT6af485yfyxuH1G3cy-euPOVBJG-VMcfa0o6PAlJCd8yUFKi_MlGZooJeqkaBnXDJ_aG6xcsY2blQVGTWMMHQaHl21GlyWUY_OU2fJj61ydux7RXoY0Hvtu4rNPaca0Eo1CqDW1mkgq5TWqHB8iLYhx_mIdV4p0xeT3_4eH4r1cuzVZtaczyT0LwGTgKmUUi_2tqa7FzDdUcAUr5QYZcp0rhTkelmL0UkfiZzEnSIvGOT1jsiBZMEoC-f34b08r8xBwFRF487C28apH0TbvHbk7T8i__S8j4F_AQAA___9_ofL), with "no 'swap' necessary." He later said the release depended on his decision to waive new Russia sanctions, a move members of Congress from both parties had criticized. # “Someone who I can turn to when times get tough.”
_-Chase Fleahman_
---
| | **Through Reed and the Bistro I found community**
I've known Reed for over 20 years. I first met Reed when I crashed his party celebrating the opening of his restaurant The Wild Hare Bistro. I soon found myself working for Reed as a cook at the Bistro. Reed took me under his wing and ignited in me a passion for food and community service. Through Reed and the Bistro I found community in the small town of Bemidji that I had only moved to a year before. Reed exemplifies the idea of Minnesota nice. He is kind, trustworthy, outgoing, and a little bit of a dork in the best way possible.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **He has consistently been someone who I can turn to when times get tough**
He will always make time for friends, and is as supportive of a person as you could hope to meet. **His work in and around the community with the homeless is just an extension of who he is as a person.** Reed lives his life as an example to others of the effect that true kindness, and honesty can have on those around you. I've been following politics since 2000 and have never seen a candidate more qualified for the office they are running for than Reed Olson.
Sincerely, _Chase Fleahman_

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Eyes on the prize
body:
We can’t put up our feet and start acting like North Carolina’s a done deal.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1719&source=&t=1&akid=4822%2E124072%2EGese6S) | | | |
---
Peter,
**I have a critical update to share with you:** Recently, Nate Silver’s Silver Bulletin has shifted his prediction for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate race further in our direction.
A lot of folks will hear that and think it means that we can rest on our laurels for these last 11 days. That we can pat ourselves on the back and put up our feet, since a win is guaranteed.
Having won my fair share of tough statewide races, trust me: **That couldn’t be further from the truth.**
While it means our campaign clearly has what it takes to flip this seat, it also means that the GOP is growing increasingly desperate to defeat me. Far-right super PACs have spent millions to broadcast despicable lies about my record on the airwaves, and BOTH President Trump and JD Vance just came for another recent hurrah to rally the MAGA base in Greenville and Hendersonville.
The tides may be turning against Republicans in North Carolina and nationwide, but Senate control still hinges on the outcome of our race. **Your grassroots support toward our daily fundraising goal is the only way I’ll fight back against any surprises they still have up their sleeves and cross the finish line first on Election Day.**
[**_So if you care about flipping North Carolina blue and taking back the Senate as much as I do, will you chip in your first donation of $5 now to power our movement to victory?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1719&amount=5&t=8&akid=4822%2E124072%2EGese6S)

Roy Cooper

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Peter,
Yesterday, Attorney General Todd Blanche was asked whether the Justice Department would try to stop states from certifying the midterm results. He refused to rule it out.
And now we know why.
The Department of Justice just sued the state of Alaska to block the certification of election results if Democrat Mary Peltola defeats MAGA Senator Dan Sullivan.
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001C7qUan-BQXIZka_aYyMqtrQ3H3q6IDyFqd4WTrDegRwKUMMfmXEkzbvc6oo7Oh_avrTnn5twH7x3kkrr1NgZFTN8BhobNtzD_drQ0NpIVaTj3oJBaGeHB9IrayLWDTl5yy1R4yUzYHIR2Beb14WivAg-9GO5CPWnx8mmE1YtW3_-MIMC1MbP2HlZ89gf06OWREy-2tUaafDgqn1hy969Tg3c_JhBMHq9f8bdKK8Ap_KHHF_E4aEJYQ==&c=LbJN0ORyzZqDxSCnRWJbE9vjSo_WOGf08UBWUldSFkqYrbbtYjtxEw==&ch=Wk8s_F0zp7eSa80Uj4y3hFt3nBEhdRkMwxwmJe3CzoO6HhvZt-5Mwg==)
---
They're trying to rig the results before a single vote is cast.
Their excuse? A second candidate on the ballot also happens to be named Dan Sullivan. He is a retired teacher who chose to run. On the ballot, he is listed as "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." with no party label, while the senator is listed as the Republican incumbent.
MAGA already tried to kick him off the ballot and the Alaska Supreme Court said no. So now Trump's DOJ is asking a federal court to do what the state's highest court would not: hand them a way to throw out the result if their candidate loses.
We need our courts to hold the line. In 2020 they did just that, throwing out over 60 Trump lawsuits that attempted to overturn the election results. We need them again this year.
This is why Defend Our Courts exists.
First, we are building a firewall of state supreme courts that protect free and fair elections. Alaska just showed why that matters. Its Supreme Court already stood up to Trump and MAGA once.
Second, we are turning out Democrats in key Senate and House races, so that when they try to steal a seat in court, the margin is too big to steal.
The coup has officially begun. With only 11 days until the election, we need the support of Dems everywhere to defend and build pro-democracy majorities on key state courts. subject: Six states. Two weeks.

body:
T minus 11 days to the election, let’s not slow down now

| | | [ ](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/216?t=3&akid=3059%2E4032634%2EY7OrvS)
---
_10/10: Michigan for Dr. Abdul El-Sayed_
_10/17: Maine for Troy Jackson and Hannah Pingree_
_10/19: New Mexico for Deb Haaland_
_10/20: Nevada for Senator Catherine Cortez Masto and Attorney General Aaron Ford_
_10/23: Georgia for Senator Jon Ossoff_
_10/25: New Hampshire for Chris Pappas_ _And more soon!_ My campaign schedule for these final weeks before Election Day has been packed — and I’m feeling energized. Six states in just over two weeks, rallying voters for Democrats I’m proud to stand alongside. And I’m not slowing down. Today, I’m in Georgia campaigning for my friend Jon Ossoff. On Sunday, I’ll be in New Hampshire with Chris Pappas. I’m doing everything I can to help Democrats win up and down the ballot, because the stakes in this election couldn't be higher. This fight is about more than who holds the majority in Congress. It’s about whether anyone in Washington will stand up to Donald Trump. It's about whether we can lower costs for working families, protect people's rights, and stop billionaires and giant corporations from writing the rules for everyone else. Trump wants two more years with a Congress that rubber-stamps his agenda and lets him do whatever he wants. We cannot give him that kind of unchecked power. We need to hold his administration accountable. And we need to fight for an agenda that puts working people first: affordable child care for every family, a wealth tax so billionaires finally pay their fair share, a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, and real guardrails on AI so Big Tech can't put profits ahead of people. That's what's on the line in a few short weeks. And we have the power to make it happen. But winning these races takes more than good candidates and good ideas. It takes organizers knocking on doors, canvassers talking to voters, and grassroots supporters helping Democrats compete in communities across the country. That's why I'm reaching out to you today. [**This movement runs on grassroots supporters like you. Will you chip in $28 right now to help power the final push and elect Democrats up and down the ballot who will stand up to Trump?**](https://act.elizabethwarren.com/go/3868?amount=28&t=8&akid=3059%2E4032634%2EY7OrvS)

# **Whatever November 3rd Brings, Thank You.**
**In just 11 days, we'll find out whether Texas has been listening.** Whichever way the pendulum swings, my message has never changed: public service is about people, not power. It's about showing up, listening, and fighting for communities that deserve to be heard.**As Election Day approaches, I want to take a moment to say thank you.** To everyone who has opened their doors, shared their stories, volunteered their time, offered words of encouragement, or simply believed in what we're building, I am deeply grateful._Four campaigns_ have given me the privilege of meeting extraordinary people across Texas. It's Chris.
I want to start with two words: **Thank you.**
There are just 11 days left until Election Day, and I want to thank everyone who got us here. Whether you knocked on doors, made calls, shared a post, talked to your friends and family, or chipped in what you could, you made this campaign what it is. I couldn't be more grateful.
But this race is far from over. We're facing an unprecedented wave of outside spending from the other side, and what we do in these final two weeks will decide this seat. Every conversation, every door, and every vote count.
I recorded a short video for everyone who has helped get us this far. I'd appreciate it if you took a minute to watch it. I've also included what I said below.
**[If you're in a position to chip in and power our grassroots campaign, you can do so here or by clicking below.](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6b0931-2cdb-4b8b-adda-f80f70a0069f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CHIP IN NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6b0931-2cdb-4b8b-adda-f80f70a0069f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks for everything you do,
Chris
[DONATE](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6b0931-2cdb-4b8b-adda-f80f70a0069f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
Hi, it's Chris.
I wanted to take a minute to talk directly to everyone who's supporting this campaign to say: Thank you.
From the very beginning, this campaign has been about the people of New Hampshire, and it's been powered by folks who believe in what we're doing here.
Whether you chipped in what you can, volunteered your time, talked to your friends and neighbors, put up a yard sign, or found your own way to help, it all adds up.
And I don't take any of that for granted.
When you're in the middle of a campaign, there's always another deadline, another event, another conversation to be had.
But I always try to find the time to stop and thank the people who have helped get us to this point.
It means a lot to me.
We've built a great grassroots campaign together.
People all across New Hampshire and the country have stepped up, and they've made this campaign what it is.
I'm really proud of that, and I hope you are too.
So thanks for your support. Thanks for your trust. And thanks for everything that you're doing to get us to this point.
I'm really grateful to have you on the team, and let's finish this strong.
Let's show the rest of the country what we can do here in New Hampshire when we work together.
Thanks.

body:

But we must not lose **hope**. Instead, we must fight back with the **TRUTH**! Hillsdale College has been engaging the Left on the battlefield of education for decades. That’s why we’ve turned our course, [**“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”**](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc-K2zAQxp9GvtnIkix7Dz6EOFn2kC7bUHoUijRxBvQPSU7Zty-G9AV6nd8wH_P7fl_URaPDsP7QHmYsRdloVYZSY8awPmICDHHLJm6h5m_FKJNtT1vGlTYVn6CEbuw8sH66Tw3M_fjGxmGkbGoes5zGEQzcJymYZhZub4O5GTCCj4PkQjQ47_d6ynjPKBeiE1wO401SOUh9sz0QQbdkdYUOQ0ELxcSYUnRY0ZQu5rVx86PWVAg_EHYm7FzAbBm6BzpXrHbQgd0IO9sYdIWdbynFXNs1g66t9pDR6NDu_3639mkJPxdYPYR6jBYIXyjvJ3mg9Hy8nN6Xz-V0-iJMbtWrsnvZV1KOJYGpGNYX8mBx84Qv4DW619BonzSugfDF6WDjfber9swXj6FCqIQvy8f1-Pnr5-H9tKivsf24Xtt_opo82_QHncMiRyLougd0Jvqm_m99z5n9DQAA___8AK1V) into a DVD set, and I’d like you to have a copy. Taught by historian Wilfred McClay and based on his published history of America, **“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”** presents a full, unbiased account of America’s past. Hillsdale’s goal in producing this course is to **restore the kind of intelligent patriotism—especially among our young people—that is _essential_ to preserving free government.** **“The Great American Story: A Land of Hope”** is a powerful counterweight to _The New York Times’_ “1619 Project,” which is injecting the idea that America is an essentially unjust nation into our K-12 schools. Friend,
I know what it takes to campaign in Tennessee. Grit. Determination. Hope, amidst a chorus of naysayers who think that Tennessee is too red to flip. An unwavering belief that our community is worth fighting for.
I know that none of that comes as a surprise to you.
**But what might surprise you is how much further your dollar goes here in Tennessee.** It’s true.
Our media markets are smaller and ad buys are cheaper. Overconfident Republican incumbents (like Rep. Tim Burchett) don’t think they have to work that hard to defend their seats.
They don’t know how to run a modern campaign and earn votes because they don’t think they have to – so every mailer, postcard, and text sent, every door knocked, and every ad has a better chance of actually reaching a persuadable voter.
All of this means that every dollar goes further in Tennessee.
My friend, Michaela Barnett, has been running a phenomenal campaign to unseat Tim Burchett.
I’m so proud of what she and her team of supporters (me included!) have built over the past year plus: 1300 volunteers. 21 people on payroll. Thousands of doors knocked every week. Over 12,000 postcards sent. Over 220,000 voters already contacted – and a week and a half to ensure that every single supportive voter gets to the polls.

To keep running as hard as she has been this past year, Michaela needs to raise another $50k by election day. In another race, that would be a drop in the bucket of a multi-million dollar budget. **In this race, it makes all the difference.**
**Will you join me in chipping in to ensure Michaela has the resources she needs to beat Tim?**

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: The greatest trick the oligarchs have played
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
I get it.
#
One of the greatest tricks the oligarchs in this country have played is to convince the working class of this country that they have the money, they have the power, they'll buy all the candidates and elections they want and there is absolutely nothing you or your neighbors can do about it.
I get it.
I come from the Bronx.
And for so long, what was so hard about it was feeling like we were growing up in a place where no one cared about us. Where no one saw us, where our issues were not addressed, where our community wasn’t invested in. And for a very long time, a lot of us would just kind of throw up our hands and just say, well, no one’s really fighting for us.
But that feeling is not unique to the Bronx. It is happening all over this country.
A lot of times when people talk about the lack of voter engagement, they talk about it as though that’s the person’s problem.
But like any other relationship in life, the relationship between a government and its citizens is a two-way street.
And today we have a government that makes a lot of people feel like they don't matter. And so why would a person step up and participate in a situation where they are dismissed?
I am here to tell you if there was ever a time to shake off that understandable cynicism and to refuse to surrender to despair, that time is now.
Because if you look back throughout the history of this country and many others around the world, real change that benefits the working people almost never occurs from the top down. It only happens when regular folks shake off the cynicism and despair they feel and act to fight against injustice.
Will it be easy?
Of course not.
Will we be successful?
There is too much at stake not to try.
First: we do everything we can to win this election, flip the House and Senate and put a check on Donald Trump's power.
Then we must build upon that success and continue the organizing work we've done not just to win an election, but to fight for a government that works for all people and not just the oligarchs spending billions of dollars in this election.
Thank you for reading.
In solidarity,
Alexandria

* * *

**🇺🇸 Wait... before you click away ⛅️**
Alexandria is not running around the country begging billionaires for campaign contributions. Our work is funded by lots and lots of people making individual donations when they can, for whatever amount they can.
The donations we do receive go toward things like the organizers we've hired in Tennessee and Florida, toward events and travel when you see us holding things like the Fighting Oligarchy Tour, or time on the road supporting Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan and Emilia Sykes in her competitive House race in Ohio.
The donations we receive sometimes go toward donations we make to candidates like Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania before he won his primary -- and they go toward worthy causes like the Northeast Bronx Community Farmers Market Project or the Bronx River Houses Residents Association.
[Can you please make a contribution to support Alexandria's work today? Our average donation is around $16. Some give more. Some give less. There is a small piece of every donation made in all of the work our campaign does.](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261023-12470-P_FND_EGR_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12470%2E2526796%2E2asWDD)

It's okay if you're afraid right now. I get it. But I need you to find your courage, because that's the only way out of this.
#

Hey everybody, it’s Mark.
A lot of tough guys out there will tell you they don’t get scared.
They’re full of shit.
Everybody feels fear. I’ll never forget my commanding officer, the skipper of our squadron, telling a bunch of us about to fly our first combat mission that they expected that half of us wouldn’t come back. This was at the beginning of Desert Storm. Trust me, that gets your attention really fast.
My wife was shot in the head, and I didn’t know if she would ever wake up. That changed our lives forever.
Everybody's afraid at some point, myself included. But here’s the truth: Courage is impossible without fear. We can’t let fear defeat us, or silence us.
It's okay if you're afraid right now. I get it. But I need you to find your courage, because that's the only way out of this.
Trump’s tried to silence me for the last nine months, and I’m not going to let him. I am not going to stop.
Can I count on your help?

Friend, Let’s talk about what keeps so many of us up at night: keeping a roof over our heads. Rent keeps climbing, buying a home feels impossible, and property insurance bills are squeezing working families across Florida. Meanwhile, Wall Street landlords are snapping up whole neighborhoods and driving up housing costs, because to them our homes are just another way to make money. I believe housing is a human right, and I’m running for the U.S. Senate to take that fight to Washington. = | | = Here’s what I’m running on: Build. Investing in permanently affordable housing, with millions of new units across the country. Protect renters. A national standard for rent stabilization, protections against unjust evictions, and legal counsel for families facing eviction. Stop the speculators. Cracking down on corporate landlords and Wall Street investors buying up single-family homes. name: Tammy Baldwin
subject: Every ballot matters.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Tammy Baldwin for Senate
body:
We’re winning this the Wisconsin way.
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5766%2E35263%2EoMcePE)
Peter,
I just voted! Early voting is underway in Wisconsin, [so make your plan today, or find your polling place at IWillVote.com](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/4420?t=2&akid=5766%2E35263%2EoMcePE).
[****](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20261023-stake.BgzX9i&refcode=em20261023-5766&amp%3Bamount=10&t=3&akid=5766%2E35263%2EoMcePE)
From governor to the state legislature, every race on this ballot matters, and every vote counts. When I won re-election, I won by less than one percent.
**_0.85% to be exact._**
That’s the reality of Wisconsin. Every race is a fight, from governor to Congress to the state legislature.
Wisconsin doesn’t like to be told what to do. That’s exactly why we won’t let a handful of billionaires spend their dirty money to try to buy this race.
**We’re winning this the Wisconsin way:** knocking on doors, building organizing infrastructure, mobilizing volunteers, and getting out the vote. But that work takes resources, and right now, every single day counts.
So yes, races in our state are decided by a few thousand votes. Every conversation at the door could be the one that makes the difference. Voters are casting their ballots right now, so our window to reach them is closing fast. Once those ballots are in, we can’t win those votes back.
**[Peter, will you rush $10, or whatever you can, right now? Your gift today goes straight into the final push for every Wisconsin Democrat fighting alongside us.](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6050?c0=em-ms-tb-20261023-stake.BgzX9i&amount=10&refcode=em20261023-5766&t=4&akid=5766%2E35263%2EoMcePE)**

Onward,
Tammy

Early Vote Action

Peter, Let me explain why I'm so fired up about ballot chasing -- because the math is beautiful. Every Republican vote we "bank" early frees campaigns to stop chasing that voter and focus everything on turning out the people who haven't voted yet. Bank 20,000 votes early, and the path to victory gets dramatically easier. And study after study shows there's nothing more effective than a knock on the door. That's what my team does -- using daily data to find who has a ballot and sending activists to make sure it gets returned. Chasing ballots = banking votes. The more chasers you help fund, the more races we win.

A note from Senator Ashley Moody |
---
Friend,
I'm going to be honest with you, because I don't know any other way to say this.
My heart breaks for France right now. City halls burning to the ground. More than 600 police officers injured in a single day. Rioters tearing the French flag off the monument to their own Republic – and raising a Palestinian flag in its place, while others march under the hammer and sickle.
Communists and radical Islamists, side by side in the streets. **That 's not a coincidence. That's an alliance.** And it has eyes on more than Europe.
This radical movement is working to infiltrate our own country – and it's counting on patriots like you not realizing it until it's too late.
It is the honor of my life to serve as Florida's U.S. Senator. My state is full of people who already know how this story ends. Families who fled Castro with nothing but the clothes on their backs. Venezuelans who watched their country get looted by socialists in a single generation. Nicaraguans who escaped Ortega. They came here because America was the one place it couldn't happen.
Here, that movement has a fellow traveler on the ballot, and her name is **Angie Nixon.**
She runs a bookstore called "Cafe Resistance." On its wall hang portraits of convicted cop killers – including Assata Shakur, who murdered a New Jersey state trooper and fled to Castro's Cuba. When she was confronted about it, she said she stands by "everything in this bookstore."
She closes her speeches with a line from the Communist Manifesto – "We have nothing to lose but our chains" – and she took that chant to a CAIR gala. She was one of just 7 votes against teaching students the history of communism. She signed the pledge to abolish ICE. She voted against tougher penalties for people who assault police officers.
And she just raised $7 million to take Florida's U.S. Senate seat – more than we raised in the same three months. And Bernie Sanders just pointed his $23 million war chest at this race and came to Florida himself to campaign for her and turn out the vote.
This is a special election – the biggest Senate race in the country this year – and some new polls say it's within the margin of error. If she wins, she becomes **the first dues-paying member of the Democratic Socialists of America in the U.S. Senate.**
| [HOLD THE SENATE](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=179ca4a17b7c4c428b0fbaae86119617&_e=D29S7w0C8eblY0zI0Lwnuwqia2tYsrUrYwyTiqyHwCZ8NsRYyFAFJXUd9hIz52iiiiDVbIO2A3WvpmK5fM3pZpn40qLoVSn-1kmZiAeD2DpurQeXHOQiqws5I0qy6KQPtNTPz6x8o282hXloJ_6L_2XeQhDXrqMw6knIBUK7_2NnFa11Tb84RIWPJHA49RM9LNXCVeENJunR8Sa_nRUKf9HPCjG_N1yV6O8TrnI0eB6dIHAzEsvVRAU0QLKmn3FBRAeHJAwwKZ-UbAN4Sd_uYfNAFhMkoqjHybSYfpMP9lL26HDubNXsPRZmI9k0bHyCsxKcJFqY4Kg9GrbtaOWrE_zmZ3mBz8iX1fRFrH-hCK9jmwBC295aN-0KqS3hUXnGXVQhMstVbglu4DkpyGuD9hGI7KGvtY6z5H4W-cACplSiqg-JkWhCdk4byjJ1tKysk1bNEVwH_UqYQO-vm8fPUelpU9YXuIifEBShwxLd3ZHVH69mD-T3az80Cg6hPYO8pxjfOl_KX0tZQp61rq3yMzcvbehV_-WL7xxKY0LeuCB302CA36z82TLMJ9nC3-egTPcOlj1Aq1awG5chx0XuyVSx4fp2UfP1FqFQpaNfVBTJe75-Dxiz89KmxOiIf3oazYU-_6y9sHmUxWG06xsEji10g_XZMsxl9gPpD0Oe0E6uJcOfE-YCQhdArFz49lNoXQOP_iKWnbxiiJGyd6tIrQzZIeBwgd-014KADgmHcQ7tlzOdVP34kQZd6z52PtzRlIUoS8I8taJqUoclMaOB_w%3D%3D)
---
My husband is a police officer. I spent my career as a prosecutor, a judge and an attorney general. I've stood with the families of officers who were attacked. I've stood in rooms full of people who escaped communism and wept when justice finally came. I made them a promise: _not here. Not in America._
**I can 't keep that promise alone.**

body:
OH-10 is ready for a change in leadership.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261023-1&t=1&akid=4184%2E587540%2Ed1F2_B)
Peter,
**The Cook Political Report just shifted another race towards Democrats.** In OH-10, Kristina Knickerbocker is going up against Republican incumbent Mike Turner who has held the seat for over 10 years, and been in Congress for even longer. Just a few months ago, this race was considered a solid Republican seat, but Kristina has been steadily gaining momentum and proving she’s exactly the kind of candidate that has what it takes to flip this red seat blue.
Kristina is a U.S. Air Force Veteran and Oncology Nurse Practitioner who has dedicated her life to helping her community and country. She’s witnessed the broken systems in this country firsthand, so she’s running to fix them. Kristina needs your help to end corruption in Washington, make life affordable again, and deliver a healthcare system that puts people first.
In 2024, Mike Turner won his re-election by 18 points. But Kristina is putting up a tough fight for the seat — just this week, a new DCCC poll was released showing Kristina _leading by 3 points_ and the Cook Political Report shifted the race from _Likely R_ to _Lean R_.
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/3952?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261023_1_knickerbocker.FKbCfJ&refcode=em20261023-4184&t=2&akid=4184%2E587540%2Ed1F2_B)
**We’ve seen this trend in races all across the country that were anticipated to be easy wins for Republicans.**
And it clearly shows that people are ready for change. It’s time for new voices in Congress. Leaders that will fight for progressive change, stand up to establishment norms, and put their constituents over corporate interests. **But this won’t happen unless people show up and vote.**
**[Peter, we’re going all in to get Kristina across the finish line. Can you chip in $5 today to ensure we get her the resources she needs to win?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/3952?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261023_1_knickerbocker.FKbCfJ&refcode=em20261023-4184&t=3&akid=4184%2E587540%2Ed1F2_B)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261023_1_knickerbocker.QKQDzN&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-4184&t=22&akid=4184%2E587540%2Ed1F2_B)**
Thank you, Peter. We couldn’t do it without you.
— David

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: One Fight
body:
We’ve come so far. Let’s go win this.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
Last week, we officially kicked off our One Fight Tour. We’ve been traveling across Texas to meet with voters, talk about what’s at stake in this election, and make sure Texans are ready to cast their ballots.
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=1&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8) | [](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=2&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)
---|---
Since launching this campaign, I’ve traveled thousands of miles across our great state, meeting thousands of Texans who feel like they’ve been left behind by Greg Abbott. I’ve heard the same thing over and over again: **Texans are working harder than ever, but getting less in return.**
That’s why I’m running for Governor.
For too long, Greg Abbott has put the interests of his billionaire donors ahead of hardworking Texas families. Our neighborhood schools are struggling, everyday costs are soaring, and the American Dream is slipping further out of reach.
But everywhere I’ve traveled, I’ve met Texans who believe, just like I do, that it’s time for change.
And now, with multiple independent polls showing us ahead of Greg Abbott, we’re closer than ever to making that vision a reality.
We’re taking that momentum on the road with one message:**There’s only One Fight this November — will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires’ world and we just live here?**
I’m fighting to make sure we realize the vision of Texas where we all have a seat at the table and the rich and powerful don’t get to dictate how the rest of us live.
If you’re with me, help me keep this campaign on the road meeting Texans from now until Election Day. **[Support our fight with a $5 contribution now.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&refcode=em20261023-2516&amount=5&t=3&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_1_tour.L2Dh97&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-2516&t=22&akid=2516%2E299639%2E5pYXd8)
We’ve come so far, but we are not done yet. With just weeks left until Election Day, every conversation, every door knocked, and every vote will make a difference.
Texans are ready for change, and this November, with your support, we’re going to make it happen.
Let’s go win this thing!
Gina

But everywhere I’ve traveled, I’ve met Texans who believe, just like I do, that it’s time for change. And now, with multiple independent polls showing us ahead of Greg Abbott, we’re closer than ever to making that vision a reality. We’re taking that momentum on the road with one message:There’s only One Fight this November — will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires’ world and we just live here? I’m fighting to make sure we realize the vision of Texas where we all have a seat at the table and the rich and powerful don’t get to dictate how the rest of us live. If you’re with me, help me keep this campaign on the road meeting Texans from now until Election Day. We’ve come so far, but we are not done yet. With just weeks left until Election Day, every conversation, every door knocked, and every vote will make a difference. Texans are ready for change, and this November, with your support, we’re going to make it happen. Let’s go win this thing! Peter, I need your help today.
President Trump personally chose Michael Whatley to run for this open U.S. Senate seat. His own super PAC and other far-right groups have spent millions on baseless attack ads smearing my name. He came to North Carolina last month to repeat those lies and rally MAGA voters behind Whatley – and **this week, both he _and_ JD Vance came back for round two.**
With so much going against me, I cannot win this race without folks like you on my side.

I’m looking for 30,000 people to sign on before midnight, and I’m counting on you to be one of them._**](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/endorse-cooper-2610-email?source=email_su_pros_jtk1720&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&askdif=25&t=8&akid=4797%2E124072%2Ee2vgOV)

I have spent my life trying to do right by the people of North Carolina.
Whether as a state legislator or Attorney General or Governor, I’ve fought hard to protect our fundamental rights, expand health care and put working families first.

| | Peter, We want you to remember these five names, because what they're doing has NEVER happened in American history: **we have five Indigenous women on the ballot in one election, three of them running for top statewide offices.** **Mary Peltola** finished 8 points ahead of a sitting Republican senator in Alaska's primary in a state Trump won by 13. _NPR now calls her race the "majority maker" for the entire Senate._ **Peggy Flanagan** could join Peltola as the first Native American women EVER to serve in the U.S. Senate representing Minnesota. **Deb Haaland** would be the first Native woman ever elected governor, and she's the clear front-runner in New Mexico. And **Sharice Davids** and **Claire Valdez** are fighting to grow Indigenous representation in the House. All five are tied or ahead. Leading in September is nice. Winning in November is better. And this is the stretch when the ads get bought, the field programs scale up, and the other side's money arrives. clean_body: Remember these names Remember these names | ~~ | | Peter, We want you to remember these five names, because what they're doing has NEVER happened in American history: we have five Indigenous women on the ballot in one election, three of them running for top statewide offices. Mary Peltola finished 8 points ahead of a sitting Republican senator in Alaska's primary in a state Trump won by 13. NPR now calls her race the "majority maker" for the entire Senate. Peggy Flanagan could join Peltola as the first Native American women EVER to serve in the U.S. Senate representing Minnesota. Deb Haaland would be the first Native woman ever elected governor, and she's the clear front-runner in New Mexico. And Sharice Davids and Claire Valdez are fighting to grow Indigenous representation in the House. All five are tied or ahead. Leading in September is nice. Winning in November is better. And this is the stretch when the ads get bought, the field programs scale up, and the other side's money arrives. It's the most expensive eight weeks of these campaigns' lives, and it starts now. name: Eric Pratt
subject: My Story and Vision for Minnesota
body:
Here is the lesson that guided my entire life.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/QM8_DuDZHk2?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
| | | | | | ,

My family moved to Prior Lake back in the mid-1970s. My dad worked in real estate, and my mom spent 25 years teaching school right in Shakopee.Growing up here, you learned early on that people look out for their neighbors. It wasn't about titles or politics. It was about taking pride in an honest day's work and showing up when someone needed help.My parents taught me a simple lesson that stayed with me my entire life: **work hard, take responsibility, and when something is broken, you step up and fix it yourself.**
---
| [JOIN MY TEAM & HELP US WIN MN-02 >>](https://us.list-manage.com/bg4CJv9fOnr?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

That exact mindset carried me onto the football field at the University of Colorado under Coach Bill McCartney, through my MBA, and across 30 years in banking and financial risk management. In business, if you ignore problems or mismanage a balance sheet, you fail. You have to prevent fraud before it happens, protect every dollar, and deliver real results.When I served on our local Prior Lake–Savage School Board, we brought those same common sense principles to government: eliminating debt, building a budget surplus, and lowering property taxes while making our schools better for our kids.Now, families across our district are getting squeezed by sky-high prices at the grocery store and the gas pump. Meanwhile, out-of-state special interest groups are pouring dark money into MN-02 to protect their far-left agenda in Washington.My campaign is built entirely on grassroots support from neighbors like you across Dakota, Scott, Rice, Washington, and Le Sueur counties.When I get to Washington, I will fight to restore economic stability, stop government waste before it starts, and make sure our police have the backing they need to keep our neighborhoods safe. **But I can't do it without you taking the field with me.**
---
| [CHIP IN $25 TO SUPPORT MY CAMPAIGN >>](https://us.list-manage.com/180PDgR_Ly7?e=905d578f8e&c2id=16eb929e7cba591464984f29a5a61342)
---
| |

If you're ready for common sense leadership that actually delivers, I humbly ask for your support today.Thank you,Eric PrattCandidate for U.S. Congress (MN-02)

I have been a first-hand witness to three disruptive moments in American politics. What I am watching build right now may be the fourth — and unlike the others, this one could go either way. | Peter,

I have been involved in three really disruptive moments in American politics.

The first was Ronald Reagan in the late seventies and early eighties. People thought he was a cowboy who did not know what he was doing. Nine years later, the Soviet Union disappeared. That was a disruption.

The second was 1994, when I helped lead Republicans to the first House majority in forty years. We had a Contract with America. We had candidates who signed it. We had a grassroots base that understood exactly what was at stake. And we won because we did the organizing work before the election, not after it.

The third is Donald Trump, a disruptor whose legacy, I have said publicly, may rival the most consequential presidents in American history if the 2026 midterms go well for Republicans.

**_[Peter, that last part is the one I need to talk to you about.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=f493781b845c40428cb74d59be1cb979&_e=oixP7vKWJ-gNKXm9lu2SS6QtdxQNlATzw7hPw83DO3UtWicAu9N89d-Io0ZNgyF23hB_8LMnuWp04GXCzSZz4pJBba-dZeMlHjtADPV1xCsbam7_n6-XRy2ot4QPKQp0AQIEirHFAtbAAPkTOj3pCP_dNcNdASur4fkzZnM9zJpXoMjLX-jODp2Sbd7YCS9NKjWJdw3CV6EBZ71-PpwiRkxmFGaVS98my9ehPmN0QIKTgRIn5ADVPxBK_ilUuXN2wByYolvn0B-y3bJPxhrupEopFeTHznOuLkDmemvCCHEpTTV5g_LoT9nq7EetoofakARxmmT1_ovQ1-rziI5qkZQTDfdK5D9GuKdeA7eASkYWY4H4ltQLVd0nzv7HFT7-lVkonRc9cmirsjHlcup_fst4Dkzp5_PAveO-XIO36MO6wsqzPYqvRtDqn6wIn80rh0a2mt_h8aH_uiYFfhbjrfEEE2j9JtXrCWzHO9nN2Fe0C2DkkzSDQKlDwPwbkdFdkOTbGFqJ3vHUQk8-tAHYs2vBCwwwaRKVxKWGLoZ8JtIZIwY1P0oo8YJR7ITmyjyWVUXsBEaWgIOFOIGGiTBybWHUSh7wEzqz8CZWSYJgkIfShlg30YjCg6QFl6L0QEchnIAJhU5_otlaQ3IaQV8I2ElxCp0aRQmy7AkQXqjfXmIIu9Bn5Zqm5Qgz3dTrq0NbVYucCRZX_BzsxdQfKRYrQHTzKeazlrJAVe2QiwZ7yg6QOq6XqyHHF549G_Cw2V1dBq3CfaT-sg8_jJGuliRSZRys1Mp9rpHcBTKbFawl11zgeMVs_CEQMtbSlK6slvjKA_HAqy51QeXmc9-RJ7zuKqUE33r_wC4RN2LExyFRP8yP2sy3x22eqVouCIJBEwSWdxZFXr8ZRtUGSDtDXrU8hwH3E9456H6cWpM0zQw7p_vutLGCW1kcsiwP-O9xbwoMTxKFYokOKTMXC7u1529Onm-Ux_lJ6YJkgiRXLIlmiHZ_HfBZCI7mx3YDhpSMcK6kSZdHZLdJ49kNqZv4o3DFOa5Mrhx82xPWoBJ6R5PF79ciJdhQZmE4uf6gwn0ACIFtrBtnahCXzmjyXX6MrNmQaQ%3D%3D)_ **

The first was Ronald Reagan in the late seventies and early eighties. People thought he was a cowboy who did not know what he was doing. Nine years later, the Soviet Union disappeared. That was a disruption. The second was 1994, when I helped lead Republicans to the first House majority in forty years. We had a Contract with America. We had candidates who signed it. We had a grassroots base that understood exactly what was at stake. And we won because we did the organizing work before the election, not after it. The third is Donald Trump, a disruptor whose legacy, I have said publicly, may rival the most consequential presidents in American history if the 2026 midterms go well for Republicans. I have watched majorities built and I have watched them collapse. I know what the organization looks like when it succeeds and I know what it looks like when it quietly falls apart. And right now, in the Senate races that will determine whether President Trump has a working legislative majority for the next two years, I am seeing something that concerns me. History teaches us that those who refuse to learn from its lessons are doomed to repeat them. I have spent sixty years learning these lessons. Maybe someone in her life is pressuring her to have an abortion. But what if, before making that decision, she had the opportunity to see her baby for the very first time? **That's the life-changing opportunity your gift to PreBorn! can help provide.** Through our PreBorn! Network Clinics across America, mothers facing unexpected pregnancies receive free ultrasounds, compassionate care, and the opportunity to hear the gospel of Jesus Christ. My daughter brought the washed greens to the table. I poured the pico de gallo over them, and as she began to mix--a jarring shift. From the television, the music in a political ad surged; ominous dread gave way to triumphant relief as the hero appeared. The music was not merely accompanying the images or words; it was manufacturing the hero.
Beethoven can carry us on an emotional journey through music alone, leaving our imaginations to supply the story. Joined to words and images, music can steer our judgment before we examine the evidence.
Emotion itself is not deception. But when music helps construct a story designed to guide our judgment, we must ask ourselves: Are we responding to the evidence, or to the feelings arranged around it?
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper. **
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

clean_body: When feeling becomes a substitute for truth. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more When feeling becomes a substitute for truth. | | | Oct 23 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- My daughter brought the washed greens to the table. I poured the pico de gallo over them, and as she began to mix--a jarring shift. From the television, the music in a political ad surged; ominous dread gave way to triumphant relief as the hero appeared. The music was not merely accompanying the images or words; it was manufacturing the hero. Beethoven can carry us on an emotional journey through music alone, leaving our imaginations to supply the story. Joined to words and images, music can steer our judgment before we examine the evidence. Emotion itself is not deception. But when music helps construct a story designed to guide our judgment, we must ask ourselves: Are we responding to the evidence, or to the feelings arranged around it? Pause. Breathe. Look Deeper. Refuel. Welcome to Sweet Ground. SHARE THIS SWEET GROUND If this gave you a moment to pause and look deeper, share it with someone who might need the same. | | ---|---|--- is a publication of . body:
Tennessee Democrats are organized, energized, and voting in record numbers. Let’s keep the momentum going. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142018632/655521522/-1746974108?refcode=261022-email&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZDQxYmI0OS1lYWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sxNPP3U-2X6UulIVHzzbQ5tGT137hXL_PccXINSjzHY=)
---
**Every single voter deserves 100% confidence that their vote is recorded accurately and counted as intended.** Early voting is in full swing across all 95 counties in Tennessee, and tens of thousands of Tennesseans are heading to the polls every day to make their voices heard. As voters cast their ballots, our TNDP Voter Protection team has received reports from voters who encountered issues at the voting machine. Whether you are voting early or planning to vote on Election Day (November 3rd), **please save these FIVE essential steps** so you know exactly what to do if you encounter an issue at your polling place: **📋 YOUR BALLOT PROTECTION CHECKLIST**
1. **FINISH YOUR BALLOT! Triple-Check Your Screen Selections:** Take your time at the voting machine. Before hitting "Print" or "Next," review the summary screen carefully to ensure every candidate highlighted matches your intended choice.
2. **Verify Your Printed Paper Ballot:** Tennessee voting machines generate a printed paper ballot summary. **Before feeding your paper ballot into the scanner, stop and read it.** Confirm that every candidate printed on the paper matches the choices you made on screen.
3. **Speak Up IMMEDIATELY If Something Is Wrong:** If the machine will not let you select your candidate, or if your printed paper ballot shows a discrepancy, **do NOT scan or submit the ballot.** Notify a poll worker immediately, explain the issue, and request assistance or a replacement ballot.
4. **Document the Details: **If you experience an issue or machine error, take note of your precinct location, the voting machine number, the time, and other relevant details.
5. **Call Our TNDP Voter Protection Hotline: 833-DEM-VOTE:** If you encounter any problem, are turned away without a clear reason, or witness improper voter intimidation, **call our TNDP Voter Protection Hotline immediately at 833-DEM-VOTE (833-336-8683).** Our dedicated team of trained volunteers and legal experts is on standby statewide to follow up, document reports, and connect you with immediate legal support.

If you ever have questions about your polling location or sample ballot, visit [**IWillVote.com**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142018633/655521523/327637188?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzEzNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZDQxYmI0OS1lYWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sxNPP3U-2X6UulIVHzzbQ5tGT137hXL_PccXINSjzHY=&emci=fa7d4798-5ace-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=0d41bb49-eace-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=6362892) or call **833-DEM-VOTE.** Thank you for standing up for your community and exercising your fundamental right to vote. **Clay Capp**

name: Andy Matthews
subject: “Is it too late?”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY ANDY FOR NEVADA
body:
Here's what we're doing now... | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5860043?e=6736d7bc47)
---
| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/1Ar5pU2GfJR?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)
---
| | Dear Peter,

Yesterday afternoon, I got a call from a campaign supporter who had a direct question for me:

_“Is it too late to make a contribution that will make a difference?”_

Given that we are just 11 days from Election Day, it’s a fair question. But the answer is emphatically NO.

Here’s where things stand: The data we’re seeing come in as to early- and mail-voter turnout suggests this race is going to be very close. It’s even showing Republicans a little behind where we need to be, meaning that get-out-the-vote efforts need to be as effective as possible down the stretch.

That’s what my campaign is focused on now, and I’m hoping you can help.

If you’re able to [make a contribution today](https://us.list-manage.com/i1RgoF2j2A8?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73), my team and I will put it directly into our efforts to contact Republicans who have not yet voted and urge them to get out and cast their ballot.

Not only is it not too late to make a contribution ... in many ways, this is an ideal time to do so.

In a race as tight as this one is likely to be, every vote counts. That’s why we’re working hard down the stretch to make sure no one sits this election out. That goes for you as well ... and so if you haven’t yet voted, be sure to make a plan to do so. (If you need information on how to find an early-voting location near you, go [here](https://us.list-manage.com/LtYzlkH_qwt?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73).)

You’ve been so generous, my friend, and I’m so grateful for your support. I hope you’ll consider one more contribution to help us reach as many voters as possible and make sure they get to the polls!

[You can contribute today by clicking here.](https://us.list-manage.com/S9CtAN_mcAF?e=6736d7bc47&c2id=6d83a76682c29c59feb3e3d11de85f73)

Thank you so much, and I’ll be back in touch again soon!

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

name: Hallie Shoffner
subject: Peter asked me to say hi
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT
body:
You might not know me yet, but Tom Cotton sure does.

# [](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/144?t=2&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
Hi there, you might not know me yet, but I’m excited to introduce myself (and thanks, Peter, for letting me say hi).
I’m Hallie Shoffner, and I’m running to unseat Tom Cotton in Arkansas. Senator Welch just endorsed my campaign, and I’m so grateful for his support as I work to join him in the Senate.
I'll tell you more about me in a minute, but before I do, I've got news from Arkansas: **national Republicans are scared of this race.**
Back in March, they said it wouldn’t become competitive. We all know the GOP considers Arkansas “safe” for a politician like Tom. But since then, Cotton and his allies have spent more than $18 million on ads against me. He just announced a $1 million operation to encourage his own voters to the polls. And just this week, the NRSC started putting money on TV in Little Rock to save him.
You don’t spend like that on a race you’re sure of. They’re scared, and we intend to give them every reason to be.
[**Will you make a contribution to my campaign today? Arkansas deserves a senator who actually cares about Arkansas, and we ALL deserve a Senate majority that fights for every last one of us.**](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=3&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
_If you’ve saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically:_

---
| [$3](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=17&amount=3&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
---
| [$15](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=19&amount=15&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
---

---
| [$50](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=23&amount=50&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
---
| [$100](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=13&amount=100&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
---
| [OTHER](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=15&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
---

---
I’m a sixth-generation Arkansan: a farmer, a business owner, and a mom. I know what it means to work as hard as you can and still worry that things are getting harder.
Peter gets that. He’s one of the Senate’s strongest voices we’ve got on Capitol Hill for farmers and rural communities, the folks Tom Cotton has left behind. Grocery costs are up. Rural hospitals and small businesses are closing. Farms are going under. And Cotton would rather spend millions on ads than show up and debate.
People here are tired of it. I hear it every day on the trail, YES, even from Independents and Republicans. This race is winnable, but their ads don’t decide it. Turnout does, and the next two weeks will decide whether we reach enough voters to win.
The establishment has written Arkansas off for years. Now Republicans are the ones sweating. Let’s give them a real reason to.
[**Will you make a donation to my campaign today?**](https://act.welchforvermont.com/go/5895?t=8&akid=1406%2E61531%2EFzJxho)
Thanks for being part of this.
— Hallie Shoffner

Turnout does, and the next two weeks will decide whether we reach enough voters to win. The establishment has written Arkansas off for years. Now Republicans are the ones sweating. Let’s give them a real reason to. Thanks for being part of this. — Hallie Shoffner | | | | ---|---|--- PAID FOR BY WELCH FOR VERMONT Welch for Vermont P.O Box 909 Richmond, VT 05477 ©2023 Welch for Vermont. All rights reserved.

| | | For Immediate Release: Friday, October 23 2026 Contact: Emma Shouldice [emma@philscott.org](mailto:emma@philscott.org)
**Amanda Janoo's Opposition to the Vermont Air National Guard - In Her Own Words** Montpelier, Vt. – In last night’s gubernatorial debate on NBC5, Governor Phil Scott’s opponent, Amanda Janoo, claimed her public statements on the Vermont Air National Guard had been “taken out of context.” The reality, however, is quite different. And very clear. Here’s the truth: In a written response to **www.cancelF35.substack.com** , Janoo said of the Vermont Air National Guard’s F-35s, **_“if there’s anything I can legally do as Governor to get them out of our skies, I’m down.”_ ** Here’s the full context: _“The F-35s are loud as hell, they disrupt our communities, and are currently being used in military operations around the world that I fundamentally oppose. The people who live underneath these nuclear-capable planes voted against having them here, and they came anyway. So yes, If there’s anything I can legally do as Governor to get them out of our skies, I’m down.”_ \- Amanda Janoo Governor Scott’s campaign spokesperson, Emma Shouldice, said: “It’s normal for candidates to have different positions on issues, and clearly support for the mission of Vermont’s Air National Guard is one of those issues. Governor Scott fully supports the Air Guard’s mission in Vermont. His opponent does not. “It’s disingenuous, however, for Ms. Janoo to claim her position on canceling the F-35s has been taken out of context. She was very clear when she told the “Cancel the F-35” substack that she will do anything she ‘ can legally do as governor to get them out of our skies’.” Amanda Janoo's opposition to the Air National Guard sets her far apart from most Democrats, Independents and Republicans. | | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

| [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&amount=7&refcode=em_20261023_10043_fr&t=13&akid=10043%2E22930333%2EbLsyVT)

Derek,
I joined the U.S. Senate in 2024, making me one of the newest senators in the chamber. We are nearing a historic opportunity to stop the extreme MAGA agenda and actually deliver for families for the first time in years.
**That’s why I’ve been visiting states across the country — Texas, New Hampshire, and North Carolina — to meet with communities that feel left behind by this administration, and let me tell you:_We absolutely can flip both the House and Senate._**
We each have a role to play as we enter the home stretch of this election. So, today, I’m going to ask you to do two things:
1. [**Consider adding a donation to the DNC — your contributions help fund their nationwide voter turnout operation and the mission-critical tech and data infrastructure on which 10,000+ Democratic campaigns rely.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&refcode=em_20261023_10043_fr&amount=7&t=14&akid=10043%2E22930333%2EbLsyVT)
2. Join a phone bank with me and hundreds of volunteers to help get out the vote:

**Phone Bank with Senator Andy Kim**
**Date:** Sunday, October 25
**Time:** 2 PM EST
**Location:** Virtual!
**[RSVP](https://ak.democrats.org/go/92781?refcode=em_20261023_10043_fr&t=15&akid=10043%2E22930333%2EbLsyVT)**
The Democratic National Committee is working around the clock to make sure that every voter can cast their ballot, from deploying poll observers to key precincts to taking Trump to court to protect your voting rights.
Meanwhile, a massive grassroots movement of Democrats are knocking doors, making calls, and doing everything in their power to make sure none of us wakes up the day after Election Day wishing we had done more to win.
**This is going to be the most important midterm election of our lives, and we need to fight with everything that we have to save our country. I know I can count on you.**
Thank you for everything,
Andy
Andy Kim

clean_body: Will you join me on Sunday? | Derek, I joined the U.S. Senate in 2024, making me one of the newest senators in the chamber. We are nearing a historic opportunity to stop the extreme MAGA agenda and actually deliver for families for the first time in years. That’s why I’ve been visiting states across the country — Texas, New Hampshire, and North Carolina — to meet with communities that feel left behind by this administration, and let me tell you:We absolutely can flip both the House and Senate. We each have a role to play as we enter the home stretch of this election. So, today, I’m going to ask you to do two things: 1. 2. Join a phone bank with me and hundreds of volunteers to help get out the vote: Phone Bank with Senator Andy Kim Date: Sunday, October 25 Time: 2 PM EST Location: Virtual! The Democratic National Committee is working around the clock to make sure that every voter can cast their ballot, from deploying poll observers to key precincts to taking Trump to court to protect your voting rights. Meanwhile, a massive grassroots movement of Democrats are knocking doors, making calls, and doing everything in their power to make sure none of us wakes up the day after Election Day wishing we had done more to win. This is going to be the most important midterm election of our lives, and we need to fight with everything that we have to save our country. I know I can count on you. Thank you for everything, Andy Andy Kim Senator, New Jersey If you gave recently via check or mail, our system may not have yet processed your gift. We are appreciative and thank you greatly for your support._

subject: I get criticism from every side. I’m not backing down.

body:
I fight for Maine—not anyone’s approval. Help me keep fighting.

| [](https://trk.emails.susancollinsformaine.)

I get criticized from the left. I get criticized from the right. And when I speak my mind, somebody always tries to tell me to fall in line.That’s not why I serve in the United States Senate.
---

I’m there to exercise judgment, stand my ground, and make a difference—not echo somebody else’s talking points.That means speaking up when staying quiet would be easier. Working to get things done when others would rather argue. And refusing to let pressure from either party make my decisions for me.You don’t have to agree with every decision I make to know that an independent voice is worth fighting for.And you don’t have to live in Maine to have a stake in this election.With the election DAYS away, my seat is on the ballot—and this race could help determine whether Chuck Schumer gets the Senate majority he wants.The votes are cast in Maine. The consequences reach every state.

subject: The Department of Justice wants to overturn Alaska’s election…before it happens
body:

Peter, it’s Mary Peltola. I want you to hear this from me:
The Trump Administration is suing preemptively to try to keep Dan Sullivan in power because they're terrified he’ll lose this race in 11 days.
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261023-3._P2AYS&refcode=em-20261023-3&t=2&akid=2179%2E1086043%2EPQKucB)
Look, Peter, I’m not used to this Lower 48 hyperpartisan BS.
It’s not how we do things in Alaska. Where I’m from in the Bush, there’s a big premium on respect. We depend on each other too much to burn bridges over political differences.
But if they think I won’t fight back when DC people try to play partisan games with our future, they’ve got another thing coming.
I’m running to take on the rigged DC system that’s hurting all of us, and I won’t let this sham stop me.
But the truth is, the only way we’re going to make sure every single Alaskan’s voice is heard over the next 11 days is together. That's why I need all hands on deck right now to respond.
**[If you’re with me, please split a $5 contribution between my campaign and Wes Moore. With lots of people like you stepping up, we can overcome any obstacle and take this fight for fish, family, freedom to DC.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261023-3._P2AYS&refcode=em-20261023-3&t=3&akid=2179%2E1086043%2EPQKucB)**

We need to send a strong message to everyone watching that we won’t let their meddling stop us. So thank you for coming together to help me do just that.
Together,
Mary

subject: The American dream of homeownership
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Phil Weiser for Colorado
body:
When budgeting is simply not enough

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142023536/655539796/1239926708?refcode=ea.c48483cf-f1ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ms=ea.c48483cf-f1ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM2MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNDg0ODNjZi1mMWNlLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Hughi7Z3keaW5mELciEAI5PjopDdAzn5ip4Ik1NimzA=&emci=3935d8b8-2fce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=c48483cf-f1ce-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=51844520) You may have heard me say this before, but when I was young, my parents worked hard to pay the bills. When I was growing up, my mom and dad were young and early in their careers. Our clothes weren't fancy, and we didn't go to expensive restaurants. McDonald's was a real treat for us. Even though they were just making ends meet, my parents were able to max out their credit cards and scrape together _just enough_ to buy a modest house for our family back in 1975. **Friends, it is _beyond wrong_ that, over fifty years later, homeownership is now out of reach for too many young families in Colorado. And too often, it is due to obstacles outside of any one person's control.** For many, rent is already unaffordable. The wait times are exhaustingly long just to get the permits to build accessible homes. And the high costs of health care and child care can make stretching our dollars to save up for a home _even harder._ **Folks, I am running for governor to take on all of these challenges and more — and I'll be ready to start on day one.** The first step to taking on these challenges, though, is winning a decisive victory on November 3rd. I know that with enough people power, we can achieve that goal together. So here's my request for you today: [**We are down to our last 11 days of voter outreach. Our state is full of unaffiliated voters who may not yet know about our movement's plans to take on housing costs, defend our rights, and give our kids a brighter future — which means we need the resources to reach them. clean_body: When budgeting is simply not enough You may have heard me say this before, but when I was young, my parents worked hard to pay the bills. When I was growing up, my mom and dad were young and early in their careers. Our clothes weren't fancy, and we didn't go to expensive restaurants. McDonald's was a real treat for us. Even though they were just making ends meet, my parents were able to max out their credit cards and scrape together just enough to buy a modest house for our family back in 1975. Friends, it is beyond wrong that, over fifty years later, homeownership is now out of reach for too many young families in Colorado. And too often, it is due to obstacles outside of any one person's control. For many, rent is already unaffordable. The wait times are exhaustingly long just to get the permits to build accessible homes. And the high costs of health care and child care can make stretching our dollars to save up for a home even harder. Folks, I am running for governor to take on all of these challenges and more — and I'll be ready to start on day one. Hi everyone, it's Charles.

I'm sure by now you have seen the vile and inappropriate attacks that Amy Acton is facing from her opponent, Vivek Ramaswamy. It's important for us all to fight back against a politics of hate -- so I am sharing a message from Amy below:
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/be861375-2628-44c8-9c96-21d9ef3a60e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I can't make this up. Vivek Ramaswamy has unleashed attack ads against me that have gone too far.
He's stooped so low that even Republicans are calling him out. He's showing Ohio exactly who he is: **a man willing to go to despicable lows to win.**
**But the fact of the matter is the polls still show this is anyone 's race. **Experts are calling our election _the most competitive governor 's race in the country, so even a few hundred votes could change things._
**I 'm urgently asking you to split a contribution between my campaign and Charles Booker to help me fight back and win this election, not just for me, but for the people of Ohio. Even $3 can make a difference.**
[Split a donation](https://substack.com/redirect/be861375-2628-44c8-9c96-21d9ef3a60e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Look, our state deserves a leader with integrity and compassion.
But Vivek Ramaswamy has proven to us time and time again that he has neither of those things.
I refuse to sit by and let a self-serving billionaire ruthlessly hurl disgusting, personal attacks at me and others to get what he wants.
**We need to send a clear message: this kind of hate and vitriol has no place in Ohio.**
But I'll be frank - we're still being outspent by a large margin, and if we allow him to dominate the airwaves for these final 11 days, we'll be at a real disadvantage on Election Day.
**I know I 've asked a lot of you these last few days. But this is one of the most important elections in our state's history. Whatever you can give today will go directly towards supporting our grassroots campaign and Charles Booker to defeat Vivek Ramaswamy. **
[Split a donation](https://substack.com/redirect/be861375-2628-44c8-9c96-21d9ef3a60e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for sticking by me,
Amy
