body:
I already have. I was ready to die doing it.
Here's a photo of the real one.
| Peter, I'm running for Congress in Michigan, and Democrats just launched a new attack ad against me. Here's how it works: they hired a little boy, put him in an oversized suit, and had him play me. The story they're selling is that I'm just "dressing the part," and that I'll never work for you. So I want to show you the real little boy.

[](http://links.mikebouchardforcongress.com/u/click?_t=bb25c0b583c5471786d790f5e4203cc0&_m=4c38534c5c8e40cfb8eacb4f80271533&_e=BCGlZahFKGMkeMichFEszWzOgJc67OomK4jll7OgN-2qvQg0gE2x_T-2mytlFhLvee6wdgkqf4zYgNgfLcU1H7rU6Nq4l1q5BE1tt_ZNpPuHZDtOml44Pdo7NNxViYpbemJJXDPRc8OctE3WSxha0shfPcbiHzHfXNEQMQuPMxIBDCqZOVWqLUZEEwlLkov7dgPd5Oqj-KOcFIi_aufI5Ze5JnLuo3P_hWNzV10BWkfVNCPW6FlSoKTNGT6h9j8d2vurCabamPq8a3MTaetpzsNhVUK6PfUi0tSk--1HUKLlVf6GssDTFEBASjx42kvLbF44omYtp6dp3XXZluXmn4wYhOCJTBbrQlowXOBHMDJGM3b3Jzn_nUQkvtAMtRBg47Ra6aF3LhY6d1G50Mmb-zfDgpB0-XE8n9v-3cvDdAAlG9WZblt3mWfctbMFVRN_ZBVMJj6vauU_8NTi_1OUFu1aAJGwGcnFqvRM-fV0GFX5Gmxuwr-_DDErWL4nMe4hLHX0FzFCnX_jc0UTpZ7pHikphdOsgZb4mgwNQEyABBdG8_fYf7JkkP5DWKa7Hd1Z6XoOHzGQ6ZRw1mIBILlsf7VVidfytcVbyAqnq7QrM8ANzm88eTgC1DYECft0WdFgRkW5UO4u2piyMQsOMPiC3_5VPwQFLwXbdTn3tvQv7is%3D)
---
That's me at six years old. No suit. No briefcase. Camo and a salute. That boy didn't dream about a corner office. He dreamed about one thing: putting on the uniform and serving his country. And he did. He was commissioned as an Army officer. He led soldiers in the 101st Airborne. He jumped out of airplanes with the 82nd. He stood watch on the southern border. He volunteered for Iraq on 20 days' notice and spent nine months fighting ISIS. He came home with a Bronze Star. They said that boy will never serve you. **He already has.** I raised my right hand and swore an oath to this country. I was ready to die for it. Some of the men and women I served with gave everything. And a Washington super PAC wants to tell Michigan I'm just "dressing the part." That's not politics. That's an insult to everyone who ever wore the uniform. So I'm answering it. I cut a response ad, and it's on TV right now:

Every day their ad runs, mine has to answer it. **I need $100,000 to keep the truth on the air through Election Day.** This race is dead even, 45-45, and in a tie the side that goes silent loses. clean_body: I already have. I was ready to die doing it. Here's a photo of the real one. | Peter, I'm running for Congress in Michigan, and Democrats just launched a new attack ad against me. Here's how it works: they hired a little boy, put him in an oversized suit, and had him play me. The story they're selling is that I'm just "dressing the part," and that I'll never work for you. So I want to show you the real little boy. That's me at six years old. No suit. No briefcase. Camo and a salute. That boy didn't dream about a corner office. He dreamed about one thing: putting on the uniform and serving his country. And he did. He was commissioned as an Army officer. He led soldiers in the 101st Airborne. He jumped out of airplanes with the 82nd. He stood watch on the southern border. He volunteered for Iraq on 20 days' notice and spent nine months fighting ISIS. He came home with a Bronze Star. They said that boy will never serve you. He already has. I raised my right hand and swore an oath to this country. I was ready to die for it. Some of the men and women I served with gave everything. And a Washington super PAC wants to tell Michigan I'm just "dressing the part." That's not politics. That's an insult to everyone who ever wore the uniform. So I'm answering it. I cut a response ad, and it's on TV right now: | But their lie has deep pockets behind it, and my opponent outraised us more than two-to-one on top of that. Every day their ad runs, mine has to answer it. I need $100,000 to keep the truth on the air through Election Day. This race is dead even, 45-45, and in a tie the side that goes silent loses. | | **The ground game is accelerating with 11 days to go.**

This week alone, Team Lawler knocked over 10,000 doors, logged 2,800 voter IDs, and made 31,000 phone calls across Rockland, Westchester, Putnam, and Dutchess.

Peter, On Wednesday night, I stood on UC Berkeley’s Savio Steps, a landmark of the Free Speech Movement, and saw a new generation making its voice heard. What they want isn’t complicated. They’re demanding a future without war. Healthcare for all. Good jobs in the age of AI. An education that doesn’t leave students buried in debt. A democracy that belongs to the people, not the corrupt and powerful. **That’s the future our young people deserve—and we need new leadership in the Democratic Party willing to fight for it.**

clean_body: Young people are speaking out. It’s time to build a movement with them.| | | | Peter, On Wednesday night, I stood on UC Berkeley’s Savio Steps, a landmark of the Free Speech Movement, and saw a new generation making its voice heard. What they want isn’t complicated. They’re demanding a future without war. Healthcare for all. Good jobs in the age of AI. An education that doesn’t leave students buried in debt. A democracy that belongs to the people, not the corrupt and powerful. That’s the future our young people deserve—and we need new leadership in the Democratic Party willing to fight for it. We can’t build this movement from Washington alone. We have to show up, listen, bring people together, and organize on campuses and in communities across the country. That’s what my Students for Solidarity tour has been about. = = = The students I’ve met, from Boston to Berkeley, aren’t waiting for someone else to fix things. They’re ready to shape what comes next. Let’s meet that energy with a politics that delivers: jobs that pay, healthcare as a right, an education that opens doors, and a country that chooses diplomacy and democracy over war and corruption. = = = Thank you for your support, your activism, and all you do. In solidarity, Ro | | | | | | | Wait! One more thing– Ro doesn't accept a cent from lobbyists or PACs, meaning our work is completely funded by grassroots supporters like you. By donating just $3 today, you’re helping us create a country that works for everyone, not just those at the top. That means a renewed investment in American manufacturing, Medicare for All, student debt relief, and a green future. If you want to support our people-powered campaign as we continue to fight for progress in Washington, please consider making a donation of $3 or more today. Todd Blanche used to be
Trump’s defense lawyer. In a 2024 court filing, his argument was simple:
prosecutors have no business making moves that could tip an election in
the home stretch.

Today, he’s the attorney general, and here’s what his Department of
Justice has been up to as Election Day closes in:

* The DOJ signed off on DHS raiding Rep. Ilhan Omar’s home just weeks
before her own election, all to go digging through her immigration
history and smear a sitting member of Congress.
* The DOJ claimed, without evidence, that some people registered to vote
in Los Angeles might not be citizens, then gave county officials an
impossible two-day deadline to check every single name. When
California refused to play along, the DOJ sued to throw out as many as
20,000 ballots.
* The FBI, which is supposed to be nonpartisan, put out a political
attack video going after Democrats, including a Senate candidate in
Michigan.
* And Todd Blanche, the country’s top law enforcement officer, has been
campaigning for Republicans at their rallies, a blatant conflict of
interest from the person who’s supposed to enforce the law fairly.

This is revenge.

Trump is using the DOJ as a weapon to punish his political enemies and
bend elections his way. And the courts that are supposed to stop him? He’s
packing them with loyalists.

None of this happens without the Senate. Senators keep rubber-stamping
Trump’s picks, putting his power ahead of your rights.

We’ve had enough. We’re exposing the corruption, calling out partisan
judges, and holding every senator accountable who votes to put Trump’s
cronies on the bench or in charge of federal agencies. This work takes
resources, and we can’t do it alone.

[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_6.OOunql&refcode=em20261023-6&t=1&akid=9736%2E582294%2EkwQ45Y)
It’s Mary Peltola. I want you to hear this from me:
The Trump Administration is suing preemptively to try to keep Dan Sullivan in power because they're terrified he’ll lose this race in 11 days.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_6.OOunql&refcode=em20261023-6&t=2&akid=9736%2E582294%2EkwQ45Y)
Look, I’m not used to this Lower 48 hyperpartisan BS.
It’s not how we do things in Alaska. Where I’m from in the Bush, there’s a big premium on respect. We depend on each other too much to burn bridges over political differences.
But if they think I won’t fight back when DC people try to play partisan games with our future, they’ve got another thing coming.
I’m running to take on the rigged DC system that’s hurting all of us, and I won’t let this sham stop me.
But the truth is, the only way we’re going to make sure every single Alaskan’s voice is heard over the next 11 days is together. That's why I need all hands on deck right now to respond.
**[If you’re with me, please split a $5 contribution between my campaign and Chris Pappas. With lots of people like you stepping up, we can overcome any obstacle and take this fight for fish, family, freedom to DC.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_6.OOunql&refcode=em20261023-6&t=3&akid=9736%2E582294%2EkwQ45Y)**

We need to send a strong message to everyone watching that we won’t let their meddling stop us. So thank you for coming together to help me do just that.
Together,
Mary

body:
| [](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=01e9e848975844ecb1692c1535203702&_e=oexCHGXSKG937k2ueLUB2ZuraXLeiBG4yzBOc91QtO3q6aKBmxJSss_LkIv5LalB2a7nD8Jxx9kvs8AnGJrXTh_aWMHvNRwvp9cSw3s7wb84jYbbnxqqwT2bUug1aNr7oXppK3hB6c1X2jRjRM5yNtZV0-h5mlhOSuhD7uL6EFdYL_RaWplQiBZV01K85-zz1WhV792kp9u8AfQ2oj2-MHAdm2YSNARQHdywqxWAEKDmuM8u-GrINsp7RPMFv4nCILqQhl05urQuAJGNxsOLuJ80mvwGt2MNx2GMdGduwnbVRWL6A_66OcHseb1u7NH2l3NDZ_Te5_7hBgjHRztRJI9Hal1Q-40XSlGgba5E_9KXQhTxzkUsj4glmNi3y5l0ziagn-AEiRLfjEUFGnOlCo_X2J7F-SS4AuvWwwKvLLgJ7T0KOd3C2k626C49YygcmEcdUKyaDAVxb0h9G4aQVf8ABuEDAXmw6U2A_3lzWCJeses1pzjSoMdu8BMdBST9gQDdTmYupKEQ0dS88c_35DvjqEV69MtYASobyKkEjE6MPUVa0xLjguHY6rv6IcVpAOspxxhW1iBbK5qZyfhiZVjLofYM41fCmUDwn7YjjkRQjsMd3KpTurgTlFdEuLxkVXBd6cWOej5Fcj7cPeSTCqiiTKpbEEr41IhyYrB-oV6PicfIRkkrgvS87U2HigtHOe2CMTy8ps3CdzwpT7sEXR9IzwwnY2Xw0DWfCGuhfQ4%3D)
---
Peter,
I know you’re getting bombarded with emails and texts this time of year, but I promise, this one’s different. I’m reaching out on faith today and praying that you’ll hear me out.
My name is Dennis Price. **I’m not contacting you on behalf of any campaign or political candidate.**
I’m a Marine who served over 19 years across various special operation and private military contracting companies, and amidst the chaotic fall of Afghanistan in 2021, I founded a nonprofit network of special operators, veterans, first responders, medical professionals, and everyday people called Heroes for Humanity.
I had just returned home after going behind enemy lines to help rescue 77 Americans and vetted Afghan allies, and it became clear to me that more must be done to fill the gap where governments and institutions fail – whether that’s in Afghanistan or Appalachia.
Why? Because I believe God calls us to put our faith into action – to go toward the suffering, defend the vulnerable, and show the love of Jesus Christ to people in desperate circumstances.
We rely entirely on the generosity of ordinary people – people like you. But when you give to Heroes for Humanity, it’s not just someone in need who you’re helping.
Yes, your support helps the flood victim who has lost everything. The child trapped in a trafficking situation. The family caught in a war zone, praying someone will come.
But today, I want to tell you about another life your gift can touch – the life of the person who goes to help.
That is why I believe **your contribution can have a double impact**. Yes, those in need, those who have lost everything and are at the lowest point of their lives, are receiving life-changing aid. But our operators, our volunteers, they are transformed as well.

My husband and I run an auto repair shop — we know what it costs to fill a tank, make payroll, and pay for childcare. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142039771/655594461/789508428?refcode=261023_RG_musk-threat&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MTcxOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjOTRmN2ExZC0wNGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=PqPSLv1XeFG8uMXAXFDlcIJoKIoT8GWTMOy7693Rrpk=)
He’ll come for us? Hold on. Let’s rewind and remember what’s prompting potential investigations in the first place, because Elon’s trillion-dollar fortune and his influence on Donald Trump have created serious problems for our country:
**▶️ **DOGE, the sprawling and disastrous pet project Trump handed over to Musk last year, not only dismantled important pieces of our federal government, cut a quarter of a million jobs, and illegally canceled billions of dollars in grants, but did it all in the most chaotic, unhinged, and reckless possible way. Not to mention their security breaches and theft of Americans’ personal, private data.
**▶️** While Musk spearheaded those cuts, his own companies were winning billions of dollars in government contracts, massively enriching Musk’s already obscene wealth and creating glaring and severe conflicts of interest.
**▶️** And just this month, his Starlink satellite service was inexplicably withheld from Ukraine, forcing a hold on all military operations and leaving their frontline troops more vulnerable to Russian attacks.

name: The WFP Monster Hunters
subject: The boogeymen buying Congress
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Working Families Party PAC (77 Sands St
body:
| | | Peter, forget zombies and ghosts. This Halloween, the real monsters are **Elon Musk** , **Jeffrey Yass** , and **Donald Trump** , and together they’re throwing more than $850 million into buying Congress.1 But the money isn’t the scariest part. **What they plan to buy with it is.** They want a Congress that looks the other way while:
* **Corporate landlords** jack up your rent year after year while ignoring the leaks, mold, and broken heat you've begged them to fix.
* **Insurance companies** pocket your premiums for years, only to deny you coverage when you're lying in a hospital bed and need it most.
* **Drug companies** force you to choose between filling your prescriptions and putting food on the table, even as they sell the exact same medications for a fraction of the price across the border.
* **Grocery chains** charge you more and more for basics like eggs, milk, and diapers while reporting record profits.
* **AI companies** build massive data centers that pollute our air and water, consume enormous amounts of electricity, and leave working families footing the bill.

And they want a Congress that does their dirty work:
* **Gutting Medicaid** and ripping health care away from millions.
* **Chipping away at Social Security** until the benefits you've earned are out of reach.
* **Defunding public schools** to bankroll private ones, and weakening union rights to give bosses more power.
* **Cutting taxes for the ultra-rich** while sticking working families with the bill.

None of this is locked in yet, but the clock is ticking. Those conversations _move_ voters, Peter. But it takes flyers, phone bank dialers, texting tools, and ads to make every conversation count, and it adds up fast. clean_body: | | | Peter, forget zombies and ghosts. This Halloween, the real monsters are Elon Musk , Jeffrey Yass , and Donald Trump , and together they’re throwing more than $850 million into buying Congress.1 But the money isn’t the scariest part. What they plan to buy with it is. They want a Congress that looks the other way while: Corporate landlords jack up your rent year after year while ignoring the leaks, mold, and broken heat you've begged them to fix. Insurance companies pocket your premiums for years, only to deny you coverage when you're lying in a hospital bed and need it most. Drug companies force you to choose between filling your prescriptions and putting food on the table, even as they sell the exact same medications for a fraction of the price across the border. Grocery chains charge you more and more for basics like eggs, milk, and diapers while reporting record profits. AI companies build massive data centers that pollute our air and water, consume enormous amounts of electricity, and leave working families footing the bill. And they want a Congress that does their dirty work: Gutting Medicaid and ripping health care away from millions. Chipping away at Social Security until the benefits you've earned are out of reach. Defunding public schools to bankroll private ones, and weakening union rights to give bosses more power. Cutting taxes for the ultra-rich while sticking working families with the bill. None of this is locked in yet, but the clock is ticking. In just 11 days, the polls close, the doors slam shut, and whoever’s inside will run Congress for the next two years. Let’s turn on the lights and see exactly who’s been creeping around the House (and Senate), Peter: 👻 Elon Musk: $369 million (and counting) Musk is the single biggest donor of the entire election cycle,2 and the closer November creeps, the more frantic his spending gets. He recently dropped $158 million on a Republican super PAC in a single check. For the richest man on Earth, that’s couch-cushion change. What he gets in return is worth far more: tax breaks, friendly regulators, and lawmakers who pick up the phone whenever he calls. Musk is the monster everyone can see. The next one prefers to stay in the shadows. 👻 Jeffrey Yass: $110 million (and counting) You’ve probably never heard his name. He likes it that way. Yass was one of the biggest political donors of 2024, and this cycle he’s already poured $110 million into electing Republicans.3 For years, he’s funneled mountains of cash into races from Congress to statehouses across the country, propping up a corporate, anti-union, special-interest agenda and punishing anyone who stands in his way. We know him well. We’ve come face to face with Yass in election after election, state after state, year after year. Every time, he’s had more money. And every time, we’ve shown up anyway. But Musk and Yass are just the ones writing the checks. The scariest monster in the house is the one they’re writing them for. 👻 Donald Trump: $400 million and a bag of candy Trump says he’ll pour $400 million or more from his super PAC into these midterms.4 Now he’s going door to door with a bag of candy, promising every adult U.S. citizen a $5,000 check if Republicans keep control of Congress.5 Don’t eat that candy. It would cost about $1.2 trillion, and there’s no plan to pay for it. Even Republican leaders in Congress say they haven’t seen one. Trump has dangled checks like this before, and it’s the oldest trick in the book: lure you in with a treat, then hand you the bill. All three of them are counting on one thing: that you’ll stay home. Because elections aren’t decided by who writes the biggest check. They’re decided by who shows up, and there are far more of us than there are of them. Every one of the 20+ congressional challengers we’re backing was outspent in their primary this year. Every one of them won anyway. The billionaires’ side buys TV ads and paid canvassers. Ours sends neighbors to the door to talk about what’s actually keeping people up at night: rent that jumped again, an insurance premium that doubled, a childcare bill bigger than the mortgage. Those conversations move voters, Peter. But it takes flyers, phone bank dialers, texting tools, and ads to make every conversation count, and it adds up fast. We’ll never match their money, Peter, and we don’t have to. We just need enough to make sure our people show up. Happy (almost) Halloween. Let’s give them something to be scared of. Two sentences have been circling in my head for weeks:
**Bracing for the worst** is not the same as expecting the worst.
**Working for the best** is not the same as assuming everything will be fine.
I keep coming back to them because I see most of us falling into one of two traps as Election Day approaches. Some people have decided nothing could possibly go wrong, and they are tiring to be around. Others have decided the worst is already on the calendar, and they are tiring in a different way, because a person who has surrendered in advance will believe almost anything that confirms the surrender. **Both are ways of not looking.**
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Every seat in the House and roughly a third of the Senate are on the ballot. This essay is not about who wins. It is about **how a constitutional people behave** when an election takes place under unusual institutional stress, and about what three words I ran on -- Care, Courage, and the Constitution -- ask of us in exactly this season.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3791e890-6795-4e41-82bf-e22c69fb96e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Where we actually stand
In mid-October, election offices across the country began receiving suspicious letters; some contained white powder, and offices in several states were evacuated. Preliminary testing in multiple places found no hazardous substance. _That does not ease the terror for the people opening the envelopes._ Election workers have been doing their jobs under immense and increasing pressure for years. The Brennan Center's 2026 survey found that **32%** of local election officials had personally experienced threats, harassment, or abuse related to their work, and more than half worried about political interference.
The conflict between DC and the states is real, too. On October 15, the Justice Department sued California, asking a federal court to stop the state from counting mail ballots associated with more than 20,000 people the government says are likely noncitizens until their status can be verified. California disputes both the list and the federal government's authority. Four days later, federal prosecutors charged 28 lawful permanent residents in cases alleging fraudulent registration and, for most of them, illegal voting. Those cases should be proved or not proved in court like any others. They do not settle the much larger claim about 20,000 voters, which remains before a judge.
The courts have been busy as well. A March executive directive led the Postal Service to create new requirements for federal ballot mail. On September 14, the Supreme Court refused to let those rules take effect for this election, leaving a lower-court injunction in place. The Court did not issue a sweeping ruling on every possible presidential role touching elections; Justice Kavanaugh, for example, wrote that the Postal Service might have statutory authority for some of the rule but could not impose it this late without acting arbitrarily. Separately, the Constitution's basic allocation remains what it has long been: states regulate the time, place, and manner of congressional elections, subject to Congress's power to alter those rules. The president has no comparable general power to run them.
And at the end of August, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs told a senator in writing that the military had no plans to send troops or federalized National Guard members to polling places, and no plans to seize ballots or voting machines. "No plans" is not a guarantee. It is not nothing, either.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=221575561&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIxNTc1NTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3OTI3NzU4NjEsImV4cCI6MTc5NTM2Nzg2MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.B5Y6KiaMsNn3o6ufA6wQiz8vUly2Mk7ynpuHT8Xgm5E)
### This did not start in October
I wrote earlier this month, in an essay called "Authoritarians Love Elections," about a mistake Americans keep making. We imagine authoritarianism as the moment the tanks arrive and the radio goes silent. Modern democratic backsliding usually looks less cinematic. You keep the election. You keep the ballots. You may even keep real uncertainty about who will win. What changes are **the conditions around the vote:** who gets treated as legitimate, which institutions remain independent, what information reaches the public, how the law is enforced, and whether the people in power accept that an election is allowed to remove them.
In that essay I followed six familiar tools: make losing look like cheating; build the data and bureaucracy that can produce doubt at scale; turn voting-rights enforcement toward election-crime enforcement; push federal power farther inside state and local election machinery; weaken the referees or change who they answer to; and use the power of the state against political opponents. None requires stuffing a ballot box. **The more sophisticated form of election manipulation leaves the count alone and works on everything around it.**
Those are real concerns in 2026. Since 2025, the Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia seeking unredacted voter-roll data; most of the cases that have reached final rulings have been dismissed, although appeals and several cases remain pending. President Trump has publicly said Republicans should "nationalize" voting in at least fifteen places. Asked whether he would accept the midterm results, he said he would if the elections were honest and that otherwise "something else has to happen."
In July, the White House removed the remaining members of the Election Assistance Commission. Project 2025, meanwhile, explicitly called for sharply limiting CISA's election-security role, including pulling it back close to elections. The administration has cut federal election-security support while state and local officials have been spending this year preparing for disruption.
And yes, I am using the word authoritarian deliberately. I do not mean "a politician I dislike," and I do not mean that America in 2026 is Russia or Venezuela. Steven Levitsky and Lucan Way, the scholars who developed the concept of competitive authoritarianism, published an essay this month arguing that the United States has crossed into that category during Trump's second term: **elections remain real** , they write, **but state power is being used systematically to tilt the playing field.** They also argue that the slide remains modest and reversible. Both parts matter.
So no, I do not expect this to be smooth. People who have spent months shouting into every microphone that fraud is everywhere, that major Democratic cities are corrupt, and that an election they judge dishonest may require "something else" in response, have already laid the rhetorical track for rejecting an adverse result. I would be delighted if everyone accepts the count with grace. **I would not build our civic preparedness around that expectation.**
The question from "Authoritarians Love Elections" was never whether ballots would exist. It was _whether those ballots would retain the power to remove the people already governing us._
This is the point where I need to say something that sounds paranoid if I say it badly: **keep an eye on what happens to our attention after Election Day.** If a major emergency erupts -- a security crisis, an attack, a cyber event, something else that suddenly consumes every screen -- do not assume you know what it is.
It may be completely real. A real crisis can also be used for political ends. In the ugliest scenario, **a crisis can be deliberately created.** I am not "predicting" that. I am saying that emergencies are historically dangerous moments for constitutional limits because executives gain room to act and frightened publics become more willing to accept exceptional power.
If something terrible happens, respond to it. Care for the people harmed by it. And do not lose track of the count, the courts, certification, or the seating of the people voters chose. A constitutional system should be able to survive two things happening at once.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9tZWxpc3NhNGNvbmdyZXNzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.9wlBAyQiJTs7acsplqnVUPpMbN-efHvZnhwLAUiT4Mc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=221575561)
### Fragile and resilient at once
The American election system is alarmingly fragmented and reassuringly fragmented at the same time.
There are more than 10,000 election jurisdictions, run by state and local officials with wildly uneven budgets, staffing, and security. That is a great many places where something can break, and in a country this size, something will. It also means there is no national election computer, no federal ministry of elections, and no single switch anyone can throw to stop a country from voting. Some of that fragmentation is historical accident. The division of authority is not.
So when someone tells you the whole system is a house of cards, ask how many hands it would take to knock it over. When someone tells you it cannot be shaken, ask how much those hands have been asked to carry. Ten thousand jurisdictions are ten thousand vulnerabilities. They are also ten thousand places where a command from Washington still has to encounter state law, local procedure, individual officials, and, when necessary, courts.
### Care
Care is the word people mistake for softness, so let me say what I mean by it. Care is infrastructure.
Democracy happens through human beings: the clerk who has been working sixteen hours, the volunteer at the ballot drop box, the naturalized citizen who has been told by a stranger online that her vote is a crime, the voter with a disability who needs a ride and does not know whom to ask, the mother who has to work out who watches the kids while she votes. Fear works by making each of those people feel individually endangered, individually confused, and individually powerless. It works best on people who believe they are alone.
Care answers by making the unit of civic resilience larger than one frightened person staring at a phone. Your neighbor knows the county election office's website. Someone down the street understands how a provisional ballot works. Someone speaks Spanish or Arabic or Vietnamese and can say, correctly, what the law says. Someone knows where the legal hotline is, and someone has a car. Someone brings dinner to the election worker who has not eaten since morning. Someone checks on the elderly couple at the end of the road. None of this is sentimental. It is logistics, and logistics is what holds a society together under pressure.
[Leave a one-time tip (thanks!)](https://substack.com/redirect/c6162541-2ecb-4925-b425-1283af779e8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### Courage
We picture courage as somebody charging toward danger. The courage a strained democracy needs most is usually duller, and harder to sustain. It is steadiness under informational attack.
Sometimes that means reading the court order instead of the screenshot about the court order. Sometimes it means waiting an hour to find out why a county stopped counting. Counts stop for boring reasons too: a shift change, a jammed machine, an evacuation, a judge. Document what actually happened. Do not supply the other five things yourself.
The most useful sentence I know for this season is short: I don't know yet. Let's verify it. This month, a copied claim spread across platforms telling voters that a ballot marked by a poll worker would be thrown out. Election officials in several states had to explain that the opposite can be true: in some jurisdictions, poll-worker initials are required. A rumor can make a voter distrust a perfectly valid ballot. What stops it is not fifteen million amateur constitutional lawyers. It is fifteen million people willing to check before they share.
Courage asks one more thing, and it is harder: do not let someone else's lawlessness recruit you into lawlessness. If somebody breaks the rules, the answer cannot be that rules no longer matter. Otherwise the person willing to violate the Constitution first gets to set everyone else's behavior.
### The Constitution
A population that does not know how its elections work is easy to frighten. A video appears announcing that "they're stopping the count," and the panic starts before anyone asks which count, in which county, on whose order, under what law. A post declares that the federal government is "taking over the election," and nobody asks taking over how. A lawsuit is one thing. Federal observers arriving under lawful authority are another. Armed personnel at a polling place are another. A court injunction is another, and so is a state official refusing a federal demand. Those are different events. They call for different responses.
Many Americans carry around a picture of the president as the CEO of the country, with an election department down the hall. That is not what the Constitution built. Article I, Section 4 puts congressional-election regulation first in the states and gives Congress power to alter those rules. Section 5 gives each chamber a constitutional role in judging the elections, returns, and qualifications of its own members. None of that creates a free-floating license to overturn an election. It means power does not run through one channel ending at one desk.
I know those guardrails are not just theory because my family had to find one. My husband, an American military veteran, spent 124 days in ICE detention. We fought in four federal jurisdictions without lawyers. A federal judge ordered his immediate release, calling the detention "flat out wrong." We won because a court existed that could tell the executive branch no, and because we learned the system well enough to find the door. The system is not perfect. It does not run itself. But it held for us, and I will not pretend that means nothing.
That experience also cured me of a certain kind of constitutional romanticism. A right you do not know how to invoke can be functionally useless. A court nobody can reach is not much of a guardrail. A law nobody will enforce is ink. Institutions become real when people know their jobs, know their authority, and are willing to use both.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=221575561&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIxNTc1NTYxLCJpYXQiOjE3OTI3NzU4NjEsImV4cCI6MTc5NTM2Nzg2MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.B5Y6KiaMsNn3o6ufA6wQiz8vUly2Mk7ynpuHT8Xgm5E)
### What to prepare for
I am not asking you to prepare for a coup, a stolen election, or the end of democracy on November 3. I am asking you to prepare for **contested information and, possibly, contested authority.**
Expect noise: AI fakes, viral rumors, premature declarations, ordinary mistakes reread as conspiracy. Expect some disruption somewhere: threats, suspicious packages, cyber problems, evacuations, local delays. Expect lawsuits. Watch especially for attempts to turn normal ballot processing into evidence of wrongdoing, or to move from "fraud might occur" to "we already know the result is fraudulent" before evidence exists. That shift matters. It stops preparing people to scrutinize an election and starts preparing them to reject one.
Then keep watching after Election Day. Counting is not the end of the constitutional process. Certification matters. So does the seating of the people who were elected. We have seen officials try to delay or refuse certification before; so far, courts and state officials have had ways to compel those duties. Do not confuse a fight over the process with the disappearance of the process.
A disruption is not a defeat. Someone yelling at a polling place does not nullify an election. Neither does a viral fake, a county that counts slowly, or a lawsuit. An official's refusal to certify does not automatically erase the ballots underneath it. One of the most dangerous ideas in circulation is that any irregularity means the constitutional process is gone. It isn't. The guardrails are not magic. They are simply things people built, which means people have to use them.
### Election integrity is not a dirty word
Noncitizen voting is illegal. Fraud should be investigated and prosecuted where evidence supports it. The Justice Department has brought real cases this month alleging unlawful registration and voting. Fine. Prosecute them.
What matters is what happens next. A prosecution supported by evidence can be legitimate while a demand directed at twenty thousand other voters can still be wrong. An investigation can be lawful while the theory used to justify a much larger exercise of power is not. Courts exist in part because those questions have to be answered case by case, under rules that apply to the government too.
That is the constitutional question I care about: whether the remedy for suspected wrongdoing stays bounded by law, evidence, jurisdiction, and due process. The lines have to matter most when the government is angry, frightened, or convinced of its own righteousness. Otherwise they are not lines at all.
### Stay oriented to one another
I am not asking you to become fearless. Fear is information. Sometimes it is useful information. I am asking you not to let it drive the car.
Between now and November 3: vote, and help someone else vote. Find out which office actually runs your elections and save its number. Learn what your own ballot requires. When something frightening scrolls past, say the sentence: I don't know yet. Let's verify it. Check on the people who run the count, because they are your neighbors, many are exhausted, and some are scared. If someone is shouting at you, do not hand them an enemy. If something genuinely terrible happens, care for the people in front of you -- and keep track of what power is doing while everyone is looking somewhere else.
A democracy is not saved by everyone becoming a hero. Most of the time it is saved by people continuing to do their jobs: clerks and volunteers, judges and journalists, parents and neighbors.
Bracing for the worst means knowing where the fire exits are. Working for the best means building a society worth staying in the room for.
**Don 't rehearse helplessness. Rehearse citizenship.**
I wrote this years ago, in another season of uncertainty, and it has been coming back to me now:

_so breathe, and take heart, and get ready_
_for change can be heard on the breeze_
_there 's nothing to fear if we're steady_
_our hopes are the same as the trees '._

It is about how a constitutional people behave when an election takes place under unusual institutional stress, and about what three words I ran on -- Care, Courage, and the Constitution -- ask of us in exactly this season. | | ---|---|--- Where we actually stand In mid-October, election offices across the country began receiving suspicious letters; some contained white powder, and offices in several states were evacuated. Preliminary testing in multiple places found no hazardous substance. That does not ease the terror for the people opening the envelopes. Election workers have been doing their jobs under immense and increasing pressure for years. The Brennan Center's 2026 survey found that 32% of local election officials had personally experienced threats, harassment, or abuse related to their work, and more than half worried about political interference. The conflict between DC and the states is real, too. On October 15, the Justice Department sued California, asking a federal court to stop the state from counting mail ballots associated with more than 20,000 people the government says are likely noncitizens until their status can be verified. California disputes both the list and the federal government's authority. Four days later, federal prosecutors charged 28 lawful permanent residents in cases alleging fraudulent registration and, for most of them, illegal voting. Those cases should be proved or not proved in court like any others. They do not settle the much larger claim about 20,000 voters, which remains before a judge. The courts have been busy as well. A March executive directive led the Postal Service to create new requirements for federal ballot mail. On September 14, the Supreme Court refused to let those rules take effect for this election, leaving a lower-court injunction in place. The Court did not issue a sweeping ruling on every possible presidential role touching elections; Justice Kavanaugh, for example, wrote that the Postal Service might have statutory authority for some of the rule but could not impose it this late without acting arbitrarily. Separately, the Constitution's basic allocation remains what it has long been: states regulate the time, place, and manner of congressional elections, subject to Congress's power to alter those rules. The president has no comparable general power to run them. And at the end of August, the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs told a senator in writing that the military had no plans to send troops or federalized National Guard members to polling places, and no plans to seize ballots or voting machines. "No plans" is not a guarantee. It is not nothing, either. This did not start in October I wrote earlier this month, in an essay called "Authoritarians Love Elections," about a mistake Americans keep making. We imagine authoritarianism as the moment the tanks arrive and the radio goes silent. Modern democratic backsliding usually looks less cinematic. You keep the election. You keep the ballots. You may even keep real uncertainty about who will win. What changes are the conditions around the vote: who gets treated as legitimate, which institutions remain independent, what information reaches the public, how the law is enforced, and whether the people in power accept that an election is allowed to remove them. In that essay I followed six familiar tools: make losing look like cheating; build the data and bureaucracy that can produce doubt at scale; turn voting-rights enforcement toward election-crime enforcement; push federal power farther inside state and local election machinery; weaken the referees or change who they answer to; and use the power of the state against political opponents. None requires stuffing a ballot box. The more sophisticated form of election manipulation leaves the count alone and works on everything around it. Those are real concerns in 2026. Since 2025, the Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia seeking unredacted voter-roll data; most of the cases that have reached final rulings have been dismissed, although appeals and several cases remain pending. President Trump has publicly said Republicans should "nationalize" voting in at least fifteen places. Asked whether he would accept the midterm results, he said he would if the elections were honest and that otherwise "something else has to happen." In July, the White House removed the remaining members of the Election Assistance Commission. Project 2025, meanwhile, explicitly called for sharply limiting CISA's election-security role, including pulling it back close to elections. The administration has cut federal election-security support while state and local officials have been spending this year preparing for disruption. And yes, I am using the word authoritarian deliberately. I do not mean "a politician I dislike," and I do not mean that America in 2026 is Russia or Venezuela. Steven Levitsky and Lucan Way, the scholars who developed the concept of competitive authoritarianism, published an essay this month arguing that the United States has crossed into that category during Trump's second term: elections remain real , they write, but state power is being used systematically to tilt the playing field. They also argue that the slide remains modest and reversible. Both parts matter. So no, I do not expect this to be smooth. People who have spent months shouting into every microphone that fraud is everywhere, that major Democratic cities are corrupt, and that an election they judge dishonest may require "something else" in response, have already laid the rhetorical track for rejecting an adverse result. I would be delighted if everyone accepts the count with grace. I would not build our civic preparedness around that expectation. The question from "Authoritarians Love Elections" was never whether ballots would exist. It was whether those ballots would retain the power to remove the people already governing us. This is the point where I need to say something that sounds paranoid if I say it badly: keep an eye on what happens to our attention after Election Day. If a major emergency erupts -- a security crisis, an attack, a cyber event, something else that suddenly consumes every screen -- do not assume you know what it is. It may be completely real. A real crisis can also be used for political ends. In the ugliest scenario, a crisis can be deliberately created. I am not "predicting" that. I am saying that emergencies are historically dangerous moments for constitutional limits because executives gain room to act and frightened publics become more willing to accept exceptional power. If something terrible happens, respond to it. Care for the people harmed by it. And do not lose track of the count, the courts, certification, or the seating of the people voters chose. A constitutional system should be able to survive two things happening at once. Fragile and resilient at once The American election system is alarmingly fragmented and reassuringly fragmented at the same time. There are more than 10,000 election jurisdictions, run by state and local officials with wildly uneven budgets, staffing, and security. That is a great many places where something can break, and in a country this size, something will. It also means there is no national election computer, no federal ministry of elections, and no single switch anyone can throw to stop a country from voting. Some of that fragmentation is historical accident. The division of authority is not. So when someone tells you the whole system is a house of cards, ask how many hands it would take to knock it over. When someone tells you it cannot be shaken, ask how much those hands have been asked to carry. Ten thousand jurisdictions are ten thousand vulnerabilities. They are also ten thousand places where a command from Washington still has to encounter state law, local procedure, individual officials, and, when necessary, courts. Care Care is the word people mistake for softness, so let me say what I mean by it. Care is infrastructure. Democracy happens through human beings: the clerk who has been working sixteen hours, the volunteer at the ballot drop box, the naturalized citizen who has been told by a stranger online that her vote is a crime, the voter with a disability who needs a ride and does not know whom to ask, the mother who has to work out who watches the kids while she votes. Fear works by making each of those people feel individually endangered, individually confused, and individually powerless. It works best on people who believe they are alone. Care answers by making the unit of civic resilience larger than one frightened person staring at a phone. Your neighbor knows the county election office's website. Someone down the street understands how a provisional ballot works. Someone speaks Spanish or Arabic or Vietnamese and can say, correctly, what the law says. Someone knows where the legal hotline is, and someone has a car. Someone brings dinner to the election worker who has not eaten since morning. Someone checks on the elderly couple at the end of the road. None of this is sentimental. It is logistics, and logistics is what holds a society together under pressure. Sometimes that means reading the court order instead of the screenshot about the court order. Sometimes it means waiting an hour to find out why a county stopped counting. A federal judge ordered his immediate release, calling the detention "flat out wrong." | Trump's allies apparently have a new plan for what to do with the democratic socialists who've won elections this year. They want the House to refuse to swear us in.
A think tank founded by Trump's budget director and one of the architects of Project 2025 just published a memo arguing that Congress should refuse to seat newly elected members of the Democratic Socialists of America. Their reasoning is that people like me can't honestly take the oath to defend the Constitution. That's a bold position to take on behalf of a president who tried to overturn the last election he lost...
On January 3, every House seat sits empty until the new members take the oath, and the House clerk runs the room. If Mike Johnson swapped in a clerk willing to play along with this scheme, one Republican objection could leave a group of elected Democrats waiting in the hallway.
The last time the House refused to seat a socialist, Woodrow Wilson was president. Now, more than a century later, they're reaching back to the same 1919 playbook because voters in Denver rejected a campaign backed by corporate PACs and AIPAC and elected an organizer instead. And voters across the country from New York City to the Midwest made the same choice.
Now, because I never want to be an alarmist, I will say that most legal experts think this plan is a long shot. But even the skeptics agree it has a chance if the results are close. Low turnout or a narrow margin gives Republicans room to manufacture doubt, and a big margin leaves them nowhere to go.
So we're going to make it big. For the next 11 days, our volunteers are knocking on as many doors and making as many calls as we can, so Denver's turnout is too loud for anyone in Washington to explain away. If anyone tries this in January, we'll be ready to answer immediately, alongside every member-elect they try to sideline.
They're betting that democratic socialists will get nervous and go quiet. They picked the wrong people.

# [Meta free cash flow turns negative for first time on $35B AI spend](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Meta shares dropped nearly 7% Thursday after the company posted its[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/66a98875-3359-448b-b18d-e900ed02d9e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[first negative free cash flow since its 2012 IPO,](https://substack.com/redirect/66a98875-3359-448b-b18d-e900ed02d9e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as third-quarter AI capital outlays exceeded operating cash generation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cash flow flips:** Free cash flow came in at negative $2.12 billion for the quarter, reversing a $10.6 billion positive result a year earlier.
* **Capex range raised:** Full-year 2026 capital spending is now guided at $135 billion to $145 billion, with the floor lifted $5 billion from the prior range.
* **Nonvoting shares:** The company is creating a new class of nonvoting Class C common stock to raise AI capital while preserving Mark Zuckerberg's voting control.
* **Credit spreads widen:** Five-year credit default swap spreads hit record highs, reflecting investor concern over the scale of artificial intelligence investment.

# [Nasdaq posts worst session in four months on AI spending fears](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Nasdaq Composite fell about 2.6% Thursday, its **[steepest one-day decline since June](https://substack.com/redirect/4f0e68ed-2bde-4952-a5e5-d79370101caf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , as Meta's spending outlook and broader AI capital concerns triggered a sharp rotation out of megacap technology.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Megacap drag:** Meta, SpaceX and Nvidia led losses, with Meta down roughly 7% and the semiconductor index posting its largest drop since July.
* **Defensive rotation:** Nearly half of S&P 500 sectors finished higher even as the cap-weighted index declined about 1.4%, with consumer staples and other defensives attracting flows.
* **Equal-weight gain:** The equal-weight S&P 500 rose 0.3% while the standard index fell, and 322 members advanced.
* **Treasury bid:** Bond yields posted their biggest daily drop in more than three years as investors sought safety amid the technology rout.

# [Brent hits $115 five-month high as Middle East attacks escalate](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Brent crude **[climbed to $114.80 Friday](https://substack.com/redirect/58c7d8ed-9ff5-4826-b2b5-f0d0bc02b4cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , its highest level since May, as fresh Houthi strikes on Saudi targets and Iranian claims of halted Hormuz traffic **[added risk premium to already elevated prices.](https://substack.com/redirect/87c8955e-e491-4437-98fa-1b923a44dd21?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **Houthi strikes:** Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh, while additional attacks hit facilities near Dammam, Yanbu and Shaybah.
* **Hormuz claims:** An IRGC-linked official stated that traffic of violating vessels through the Strait of Hormuz had been completely stopped after tanker strikes.
* **Aramco evacuation:** Saudi Aramco ordered an evacuation of its Dhahran headquarters, the first such move since the current conflict began.
* **Futures pressure:** Equity futures slipped as the oil spike compounded Thursday's AI-led selloff, with WTI also rising above $100.

# [Moderna plunges 18% as leaked melanoma vaccine data disappoints](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Moderna shares fell more than 18% Thursday after late-stage trial data for its personalized melanoma vaccine with Merck[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/34446f03-7f1f-47a5-b439-8fc3a022b2e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[leaked online,](https://substack.com/redirect/34446f03-7f1f-47a5-b439-8fc3a022b2e6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** sparking a sell-the-news reaction that **[erased roughly $24 billion in market value.](https://substack.com/redirect/00a48a01-557c-42e8-8be6-b98965fb0b4b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Efficacy numbers:** The combination of Intismeran and Keytruda cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% and distant metastasis or death by 38% versus Keytruda alone in a trial of more than 1,100 patients.
* **Timing of leak:** Detailed results surfaced on an oncology site ahead of the planned European Society for Medical Oncology presentation in Madrid.
* **Oncologist view:** Physicians described the data as solid and clinically meaningful, creating a rare disconnect with the sharp Wall Street selloff.
* **Prior expectations:** The stock had more than quintupled year-to-date after earlier interim results showed meaningful reductions in recurrence risk.

# [New Mexico judge hits Meta with $25 billion privacy penalty](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **Named executives:** The decision referenced Mark Zuckerberg and Sheryl Sandberg in connection with the practices at issue.

* **Market reaction:** The ruling added to an already difficult session for Meta shares driven by AI spending concerns.

# [Meta cuts deal so Zuckerberg stays in California despite wealth tax](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
An October 21 filing shows Mark Zuckerberg considered relocating from California **[over the proposed one-time 5% billionaire tax](https://substack.com/redirect/4050210f-9eb0-485e-9d6e-000b302911f5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but agreed to keep his primary residence in the state under a board-approved share arrangement.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f70d88c5-9cb9-4059-869e-9a29e5a53250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Residency commitment:** The agreement keeps Zuckerberg in California for eight years if Proposition 40 passes.
* **Control protection:** The new nonvoting share class helps him address potential tax liabilities without diluting his roughly 61% voting stake.
* **Economic ownership:** Zuckerberg holds about 13% of Meta's economic interest while controlling the majority of votes.
* **Timing:** The arrangement was reached with less than two weeks remaining before the midterm elections.

But I need you to hear this: The election that will determine whether our Republic reaches 2028 intact is this November.
_In 11 days._
I’m serious: These midterms are vital to our Republic’s future.
_So much is on the line._
And my Senate race in Georgia will be one of the most important and consequential in the nation.
So don’t wait until 2028. Investing in this race is something you can do _right now_ to make a real difference and send a massive message to Trump and my MAGA extremist opponent Mike Collins that we’re ready to fight for our country’s future.

Billions from foreign princes and oligarchs ... sweetheart real estate deals all over the world ... tax dollars supporting Trump-backed companies.

That's the party my parents raised me to respect.That party is gone. What's left is a party that no longer asks whether something is true, only whether it's loyal. name: Andy Beshear
subject: My thoughts on what’s happening in New Hampshire
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
Chris Pappas is in a close race — and Republicans are coming for this seat.
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_3.Znqbxz&refcode=em20261023-3&t=1&akid=9697%2E582294%2ENUKBBg)
Hi, it’s Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear.
There’s a lot of noise in an election year — I know that better than most. **But let me be very clear: The Senate race in New Hampshire could decide the direction of this country.**
Chris Pappas is running in a close race. It’s been rated a Toss Up. And with Donald Trump in the White House, the stakes couldn’t be higher.
**[That’s why I’m asking you to donate right now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_3.Znqbxz&refcode=em20261023-3&t=2&akid=9697%2E582294%2ENUKBBg)**
The first year of this second Trump Administration has seen chaos, division, and dangerous rollbacks of basic freedoms. That’s why it’s so important that we elect leaders like Chris Pappas — leaders who know how to bring people together, deliver real results, and who will never forget who they’re fighting for.
Chris’s opponent is a former U.S. Senator with national name recognition and the backing of national Republicans and their deep-pocketed super PACs. Republicans believe they can flip this seat and block any chance that we have of checking Trump’s power in Washington.
But I believe in Chris — and I believe we can win.
Chris understands that leadership isn’t about grabbing headlines or scoring political points. It’s about showing up, listening, and doing the hard work to deliver for working families. He’s done that in Congress, and I know he’ll bring that same spirit of public service to the Senate.
Kentucky and New Hampshire may look different, but our people want the same things: good jobs, strong public schools, access to health care, and a better future we can build together. That’s what Chris Pappas is fighting for. **_But he can’t do it alone._**
**[If you’re with me — and ready to stop Trump and his allies from flipping this critical seat — contribute now to help Chris Pappas win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_3.Znqbxz&refcode=em20261023-3&t=3&akid=9697%2E582294%2ENUKBBg)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261023_3.Znqbxz&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-3&t=22&akid=9697%2E582294%2ENUKBBg)**
Thank you for standing up and stepping in when it counts.
Let’s get Chris across the finish line.
Thank you,
Andy Beshear
Governor of Kentucky
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**

body:
Turnout is up from 2022. Here’s what the numbers mean. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142046425/655612178/439559405?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzY3NjA5OWEtMGZjZi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=yFbix3nNN8EH_qhYev8ApcZxm4nbr6e0GfLk3AnLlK4=)
Friend, Our data team just sent over the latest numbers on ballots returned in CA-45, and we wanted you to see them before the weekend. | CA-45 Early Vote | 2026 | 2022, same day
---|---|---
Turnout | 11.5% | **9.6%**
Ballots cast | 51.9k | **40.7k**
**** updated 10/23/26 ****
Turnout is already ahead of where it was at this point in 2022, which tells us voters here are paying attention.
Around 395,000 ballots are still sitting at home across CA-45, which means the vast majority of voters haven’t weighed in yet. Two years ago, this was the second-closest House race in the country -- determined by just 653 votes. We’re not assuming this one will be any different.

Fellow Patriot -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**
How long I've been in this race.
I did not seek this moment, Fellow Patriot. I never thought I'd be in this position. Politics was Lindsey's thing. But when President Trump asked me to run for a full Senate term, I knew I had to answer the call to, once again, serve the people of South Carolina.

Since entering, I am running my third statewide campaign in just three months. I know so many of you have been so generous to help me, but it's taken its toll. Our campaign is running on fumes.

**RCP Average: +2.7:**
**Darline Graham: 48%**
**Annie Andrews: 45.3%**
This is the average of all the recent polls in the South Carolina Senate races. We're only up by 2.7%.

Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PACs have spent millions attacking me, spreading lies about my family and me. She's also lying about where she stands on the issues. She's wearing a "moderate mask" that will disappear IF she's elected to the Senate to stand with Chuck Schumer, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed.

I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. We’ve come a long way together since we began this journey. **Five years ago, I had never run for office.**
I was an Army Captain who ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country. I listened to your stories, and we all saw the same thing:

It's Stephanie Grisham reaching out to you for the very first time. In a moment, I'm going to ask you to make a donation to Adam Hamilton's
Senate campaign in Kansas. But first, let me explain why I'm supporting him.
As White House press secretary during President Trump's first administration, I learned what really goes on behind the scenes in Washington. I saw the chaos, corruption and dishonesty up close, and I saw what it cost real people. Once you've seen that, you can't unsee it.
I had a choice to make. When staying in the White House meant putting my political party and the president over my country, I resigned. **Adam 's campaign caught my attention because he has the same conviction of putting country before party and people over politics, along with a long history of building bridges and bringing people together. And as a Kansas voter, that's why he has my support.**
**What 's more, I've seen the polls showing he can win and the election experts shifting the race to a toss-up. [That's why I'm reaching out to you today asking you to support his campaign. With our help, Adam can flip this seat and get to work fixing what's broken in Washington. If you're with me, will you chip in anything you can spare or more now to help him win?](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/2c720129-25e6-4d38-ba42-5ffa9f9dd1d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
When I left the Trump White House, I moved to Kansas. After living here for the past five years, I consider myself a Kansan. And I work hard every day to live up to our values: to help my neighbors, live with honesty and integrity and make the world a better place for everyone.
I've watched Sen. Roger Marshall turn his back on my fellow Kansans. He's a rubber stamp for the president. He's refused to hold a town hall for over 500 days. And he spent thousands of dollars of taxpayer money on visits to his beach house in Sarasota, Florida. He's more interested in serving himself and party bosses than the people of Kansas.
This is not the leader that Kansans need or deserve. We're ready for a leader who knows we're stronger when we work together. We're ready for a leader who will live and lead with integrity, stand up to the corruption in Washington and put Kansans first.
**Adam Hamilton is that leader.** He's a longtime pastor who has spent decades listening to Republicans, Democrats and Independents, thinking critically about how to make their lives better and standing up for them even when it's hard. He's independent-minded, and we need that kind of leadership now more than ever.

Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 11 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=10031%2E22930333%2EzXecUp). That means investing in state parties, mobilizing over one million grassroots donors to counter Republican megadonors, expanding direct digital outreach, and supporting boots-on-the-ground organizing in must-win battleground races. [**Since you're one of our most engaged supporters I'm personally asking you to consider chipping in $7 to the DNC TODAY. We only have 11 days to execute our strategy and win big.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&amount=7&refcode=em_20261023_10031_fr&t=6&akid=10031%2E22930333%2EzXecUp) Thank you again, Ken

Please take a few minutes to read it if you can.** \--------------------------------------------------
**To:** Derek Willis**
**From:** The Desk of the DNC Chair, Ken Martin
**Date:** October 22nd, 2026
**Subject:** State-of-the-Midterms Update There are 12 days until Election Day, and Democrats have a real chance at taking back control of both the House and Senate this November. Here’s what we’re doing to make that happen:
* **Democrats need to flip four Republican-held seats to win the Senate.** A Democratic Senate majority would shatter Donald Trump’s trifecta and make sure he _never_ gets to appoint another right-wing hack to the Supreme Court again. That’s why the DNC is sending record-breaking investments to Democratic state parties: to help them make the biggest voter contact push in midterm history and flip these seats.
* **The DNC is mobilizing more than one million Americans to fight back against GOP billionaires attempting to buy our democracy.** GOP megadonors and super PACs plan to spend nearly **1 BILLION dollars** in House, Senate, and down-ballot races to ensure that Republicans keep their trifecta. They know that if Democrats win control of Congress, their far-right agenda will come to a screeching halt. But while Republicans have MAGA billionaires on their side, our movement is powered by hardworking Americans — teachers, nurses, and truck drivers — who are pitching in an average of $34.32 at a time to support our efforts and help us build the infrastructure necessary for Democrats to win.
* **The DNC is countering the influx of MAGA attack ads with direct digital outreach.** For years, people have asked when Democrats will step up their online presence. We’ve done just that. The DNC has a brilliant team of social media strategists working to expose Trump’s and MAGA’s lies online. We just recently reached 14.4 million total followers and generated over 1 billion impressions across social media platforms. This massive organic and targeted online reach allows us to bypass legacy media channels and communicate directly with swing voters and grassroots supporters alike.
* **The DNC is putting boots on the ground and organizing in key battleground states.** Through specialized training bootcamps, sharing our DNC Campaign Playbook, hiring campaign fellows, and hosting local listening tours, we’ve trained hundreds of field organizers, registered tens of thousands of voters, and empowered Democratic state parties and campaign staff to fight and win next month.

\--------------------------------------------------

We’ll put your donation to work immediately to fund all the work I just told you about — and more — to elect Democrats across the country.**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.AWsDfI&amount=7&refcode=em_20261023_10031_fr&t=8&akid=10031%2E22930333%2EzXecUp) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261023_10031_fr&t=9&akid=10031%2E22930333%2EzXecUp)**

On Monday I debated Congressman Jim Himes and the Independent Candidate Benjamin Wesley. I am attaching the link to the debate.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/445825ae-111f-46e6-a40d-d8253d4629d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A lot of issues were discussed including socialism. The Democrat Socialist Agenda would lead to the end of American Democracy. They want to eliminate the President, the Senate, the Supreme Court and trash the Constitution. They want to eliminate private property, and have the government take over our industries. Could you imagine Bernie Sanders running the airline industry or AOC running Amazon.
There are currently at least 4 socialist in the Congress and 4 more are coming. Jim Himes has always had socialist leanings though he hides them very well. Whether you like it or not Mandani and El Sayed are on the ballot.
Currently when pass away you can gift to your heirs up to $15 million tax free. You can give your house, your business or other assets to your heirs tax free if they stay under the limits.
Jim Himes does not think that is fair and believes that you should pay taxes on anything you inherit from your parents. For example under Himes if you inherited your parent's house the government gets a piece and you would have to take out a mortgage to keep the house. The house was paid for with after tax dollars, although the interest is deductible, the government did not mow the lawn, or shovel the snow or make repairs or upgrades yet Himes wants to make the government your partner and co-owner of the house that you would have to buy out when your parents die and leave you the house.
To me this is ridiculous as are many of his other ideas.
He does not serve the interests of the people of Connecticut. Where are the federal dollars to fix I95 or the Metro North. Eighteen years ago he promised to fix the approximately 100 foot long Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport and it is still not done. He exported 400 postal jobs to White Plains NY and now our mail is sorted in NY not Connecticut.
We deserve better.
I am fighting an uphill battle against an entrenched congressman with bad ideas, because I am fed up with how we have been shortchanged in Connecticut. We send a lot of tax money to Washington and thanks to Himes we get very little back.
We have been writing this Substack with the sole purpose of sharing our ideas and information with the people who subscribe.
**Today is different I am asking for your support to help me win this election.**
**If you want to fight for change I need to raise some money to fight back.**
Time is running out early voting has already started.

I am attaching the link to the debate. A lot of issues were discussed including socialism. The Democrat Socialist Agenda would lead to the end of American Democracy. They want to eliminate the President, the Senate, the Supreme Court and trash the Constitution. They want to eliminate private property, and have the government take over our industries. Could you imagine Bernie Sanders running the airline industry or AOC running Amazon. There are currently at least 4 socialist in the Congress and 4 more are coming. Jim Himes has always had socialist leanings though he hides them very well. Whether you like it or not Mandani and El Sayed are on the ballot. Currently when pass away you can gift to your heirs up to $15 million tax free. You can give your house, your business or other assets to your heirs tax free if they stay under the limits. Jim Himes does not think that is fair and believes that you should pay taxes on anything you inherit from your parents. For example under Himes if you inherited your parent's house the government gets a piece and you would have to take out a mortgage to keep the house. The house was paid for with after tax dollars, although the interest is deductible, the government did not mow the lawn, or shovel the snow or make repairs or upgrades yet Himes wants to make the government your partner and co-owner of the house that you would have to buy out when your parents die and leave you the house. To me this is ridiculous as are many of his other ideas. He does not serve the interests of the people of Connecticut. Where are the federal dollars to fix I95 or the Metro North. Eighteen years ago he promised to fix the approximately 100 foot long Congress Street Bridge in Bridgeport and it is still not done. He exported 400 postal jobs to White Plains NY and now our mail is sorted in NY not Connecticut. We deserve better. I am fighting an uphill battle against an entrenched congressman with bad ideas, because I am fed up with how we have been shortchanged in Connecticut. We send a lot of tax money to Washington and thanks to Himes we get very little back. body:
It's Governor Wes Moore.
**President Trump barred me from speaking at an event in Baltimore** , but he can’t stop me from standing up for Maryland.
We were set to announce plans for a manufacturing facility that will create thousands of good-paying, permanent jobs before the Trump administration barred me from speaking at the event.
**I won’t bow to anybody** — and I won’t let Trump stop us from delivering for people. While he’s playing politics, I’m proud to say this deal is the largest private investment in Maryland in over a decade and these jobs will bring work, wages, and wealth to our state.
That’s because I’m committed to making progress for everyone, and together, we’re continuing to make sure we leave no one behind.
But I need you with me to stay in this fight. My opponent is Trump’s man in Maryland and we have less than two weeks left in this race to defeat him.

Friend, President Trump just told his supporters exactly what this election is about. His words: **_“Please pretend I’m on the ballot.”_** He isn’t. But his agenda is, along with the House majority that decides whether anyone holds him accountable. Costs are still too high, and the war he started still isn’t over. Instead of taking responsibility for any of it, he’s asking voters for a blank check: more MAGA Republicans in Congress to cover for him. Meanwhile, he and his allies keep attacking the right to vote itself. That’s why I just joined the Democratic Party of Illinois at a voter protection event to discuss those attacks and make sure voters have the facts and a plan to make their voices heard. We the people choose our leaders, and every vote deserves to be counted. | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142048301/655619109/-489362013?refcode=em-10.23.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjQwNyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxYjg1ZWYwOS0xNGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=b5SyQPslCiVmgB2RqoIZck50hcDNLX9bgp5v1KX0n_A=)

Here’s what Republicans say about this race when they think no one’s listening.

For once, we agree with Ken Paxton. At a private fundraiser with lobbyists in Washington last month, Paxton was asked about the governor’s race. Here’s what he said, on tape: **“Yes, Abbott is struggling.”** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142049546/655623146/1757930043?amounts=5,10,15,25,50,100,250&refcode=email_102326_hinojosa&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83MjY1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMjg0YmIxZi0xNmNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MqngIB5rFXPBCseRvVD-Fq1r8pMC6eRofGcGQQXLZUc=) _Audio obtained by Rolling Stone_ He went on to admit that even with all of Greg Abbott’s money and name recognition, this race is close. In public, they act like this race is a done deal. **In private, they’re telling their donors it’s a fight.** Greg Abbott has raised over $141 million and spent over $120 million trying to stop us.
