body:
This is the sixth poll in within a month with us ahead, but Abbott still has way more cash to spend.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, a recent poll just came out showing me at 48% and Greg Abbott at 47%:
**That's the sixth poll in the last month with us ahead.** A few months ago, plenty of people didn't think we'd be anywhere near this close to flipping Texas.
But we can’t waste a second celebrating. One point is well within the margin of error, and 5% of voters are still undecided. **This race is a true toss-up, and what happens in the next few days will determine how it ends.**
So far in this race, Abbott has outspent us 10 to 1, putting most of a $106 million war chest into ads, and we are still tied. That’s remarkable. It means that he hasn’t been able to buy an insurmountable lead in this race, and your support has kept us competitive.
_**But he still has plenty of money left, and that’s a problem.**_ The latest campaign finance reports recently dropped:
Cash on hand: TX-GOV
🔴 Abbott — $17.3 million
🔵 Hinojosa — $4.1 million
He has more than four times as much cash on hand as we do, and he's going to spend it all. Early voting ends in just 7 days. Between now and then, the undecided voters who will decide this race are going to see a lot of Greg Abbott ads, _and I need to make sure they hear from us too._
If you've been meaning to give and haven't yet, now is the time. We've never needed you more. **[Can you chip in before early voting ends to help us stay competitive in the final weeks of this race?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_4_yougov.5QSsWF&refcode=em20261023-2521&t=2&akid=2521%2E299639%2EqG-Esx)**

Thank you,
Gina

clean_body: | | | | = I’ve been hearing from a lot of people who are energized and motivated to break Trump’s trifecta in just 11 days, but aren't exactly sure what to do with all that energy in these final days. So if that’s you, here's my three-step plan for anyone who's ready to help build the blue wave we all want: 1\. Have a conversation. Think about every person in your life who doesn't usually vote — or doesn't usually vote Democratic — and reach out to them! Listen to them, and then make your sincere case for why they should vote blue. Personal conversations are more powerful than we give them credit for, and you don't have to agree on everything to agree on one key vote. 2\. Volunteer. Whether that's knocking on doors or making calls from home, there are still so many opportunities to plug in. Your state or county , , and are all great places to start. And taking concrete action is genuinely one of the best antidotes to election anxiety. 3\. Chip in (yes, really). Grassroots donations are a huge deal for campaigns. No matter the amount, they can truly impact the budgets that get approved, the work that gets done, and the voters that can be reached — meaning they can be the difference between winning and losing. If you can contribute to my campaign, I can promise you every dollar goes toward flipping the House: both winning my own race and supporting vulnerable frontline members and Democratic challengers in seats we need to win. = Whether you take all three steps or just one, please take action, and remind everyone you know that complacency is not an option! It's going to take all of us to get this done — and I can't wait to see what we build together in 11 days. — Sara = | | | Congresswoman Sara JacobsCalifornia’s 51st District = | = Paid for by Sara Jacobs for Congress Sara Jacobs for Congress PO Box 120085 San Diego, CA 92112 United States | | | | | | ---|---|--- We believe these emails are a critical way for Sara to stay in touch with supporters and constituents. # One Final Ask Before Election Day
---
We're entering the final days of this campaign, and I'm asking for your help one more time.
Over the past year, I've traveled across South Dakota, listening to voters, hearing their concerns, and talking about what our state needs from its next representative in Congress. We've covered thousands of miles, knocked on doors, and had conversations in communities across the state.
But our work isn't finished.
We need the resources to keep our advertising running, reach voters who haven't heard from us yet, and make sure our message is getting in front of South Dakotans before they cast their ballots.
That's why I'm asking you to make one final contribution today.
I've given this campaign everything I've got, and I'm ready to keep working right up until the polls close on November 3.
Thank you for standing with me.
---

# South Dakota by the Numbers
---
When I launched this campaign on September 8, 2025, I made a commitment to visit all 66 counties in South Dakota. I knew it would mean a lot of miles, oil changes and long days. What I didn’t know is just how much I would learn from the people I met along the way.
66 counties. 41,742 miles (to date). 47 town halls. Over 4,000 doors knocked.
From Buffalo to North Sioux City, Rosholt to Edgemont, I’ve had the privilege of listening to South Dakotans from every walk of life. Farmers and ranchers, teachers, healthcare workers, small business owners, retirees, and young families have shared their stories, frustrations, policy ideas, and hopes for the future.
Many of these conversations will stay with me forever.
---

# Postcard Party this Sunday!
---
Join us for a postcard-writing party from 3:00-5:00 pm at Campaign Headquarters (1737 S. Cleveland Ave., Sioux Falls) as we work to reach voters in the final days before Election Day! We'll be writing postcards in support of Nikki Gronli and Dan Ahlers, and we'd love to have you join us.
No experience necessary — just come ready to write! Pizza and soda will be provided.
---

# Upcoming Events

#### October 24 | 1:00-3:00 PM | Door Knock with Nikki!
---
Join me for an afternoon of door knocking as we work to reach voters in the final days of the campaign! We'll meet at campaign headquarters for instructions before heading out into the community.
---
#### October 28 | 6:00 PM | Boos & Ballots

I'll be joining the Young Democrats of South Dakota for their Boos & Ballots event, a Halloween-themed candidate meet and greet!
Come connect with local and statewide candidates, meet other South Dakotans, and enjoy an evening of conversation before Election Day.

# Make Your Plan to Vote!
---
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, and it's time to make your plan to vote! Whether you're voting early or heading to the polls on Election Day, take a few minutes now to make sure you're ready.
* Check your polling location. Make sure you know where to go on Election Day.
* Decide when you'll vote. Early voting is already underway in South Dakota!
* Make sure you're prepared. Check your voter information and bring an acceptable form of identification.
* Remind your friends and family. Make sure the people in your life have a plan to vote, too.

Hi Friend,
Tomorrow is going to be something special, and I do not want you to miss it.
This Saturday, we are bringing the whole VA-10 family together for our Get Out the Vote rally, and I wanted to personally invite you to be part of it.
**Saturday, October 24th at 11am**
**Office of Elections, 750 Miller Dr., Leesburg, VA 20175**
[](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
We'll have great food, great music, great speakers, and neighbors who believe our community deserves better, all in one place. Families, veterans, first-time volunteers, and longtime supporters will be standing together, r _eady to finish this race the right way_.
**You have helped build this movement.** You have given your time, your voice, and your belief in what we can do. Now it is time to celebrate that together and get fired up for the final stretch.
_**Come energized to vote for a new voice for VA-10 and to vote NO on all 3 amendments.**_
Bring your spouse, your kids, your friends, and anyone who needs a reason to feel hopeful about this election. The more, the better!
**Join us,[RSVP HERE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.) and let us know you are coming!**
I cannot wait to see you tomorrow. Come be part of it!
| | | God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

clean_body: Our state & local candidates need our help to get over the finish line. | = Peter, across the country, Democratic pro-choice women are running in state and local races that could come down to just a handful of votes — and they need our help to get over the finish line. = | = Here are some of the women counting on us: Dr. Racquel "Rockee" Armstrong (AZ-LD13) — Rockee is an educator and school administrator running to flip a critical Arizona legislature seat. Winning this seat is one of our best shots to secure Democratic control of the Arizona state legislature for the first time in decades. Dr. Theresa Brooks (MI-SD09) — As a physician, small business owner, and current Troy City Council member, Theresa has spent her career fighting to keep Michigan families safe and healthy. Now, she’s running to flip a critical seat to help Democrats hold the state Senate. Sara Agerton (PA-HD88) — Sara has spent her career in social work helping children in the foster care system and serving patients in end-of-life hospice care. That’s where she learned that the system is failing us. Now, she’s running for the Pennsylvania state House to fix it and deliver for Pennsylvanians. Becky Nichols (WI-AD53) — Becky is an active member of the Menasha community and served on the city council for 12 years. Now, she’s part of our slate working to flip the Wisconsin state Assembly. Case File No DRT-ED-REVIVAL · Special File · The Desert Comeback
Everyone Said American Energy Had Peaked. A Power Plant in the Utah Desert Just Switched On.
In September, a new kind of power plant in southwestern Utah began delivering electricity to the grid. One of the world’s largest tech companies has already signed up for nearly 400 megawatts of its output. The project’s backers say it could eventually power about 350,000 homes. Most investors haven’t noticed.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded
| | | | | | | | |
---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---
|
---
For years, the story of American energy was supposed to be decline: old plants closing, fights over pipelines, a grid struggling to keep up. Then AI arrived, demand for electricity started climbing again, and companies began looking in places nobody expected. One of those places is a patch of desert in Utah.
The evidence board
| | What Just Happened
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — first power.** On September 24, 2026, the developer of a large energy project in southwestern Utah announced that its first unit had started producing power. The first phase is about 100 megawatts, with 500 megawatts planned in total.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the buyer.** Earlier in September, one of the world’s largest tech companies signed a deal for 396 megawatts from the project, with an option to expand to close to 1 gigawatt by 2030.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the money.** In March, the project closed $421 million in financing. Crews there have drilled wells more than three miles deep in about 16 days.
| OUR THEORY
---
AI needs electricity that runs 24 hours a day, every day, regardless of the weather. Very few sources can deliver that without fuel. When one starts working at scale, the companies behind it, and the ones supplying it, can become some of the most valuable in the energy business.
Connected file
| | The Real Limit on AI
---|---
Chips get the attention, but electricity may be the tighter constraint. A single AI supercomputer, Colossus 1 in Memphis, draws more than 300 megawatts. The EIA expects U.S. power demand to keep setting records, and utilities in many regions are struggling to keep up.
That’s why some analysts believe a new “energy elite” is forming around whoever can supply AI’s power.

clean_body: I am not a career politician. I am stepping up to serve again because Montana is my home. | Fellow Patriot, Early voting is already underway in Montana. Election Day is 11 days away. I want to make sure you know exactly who is asking for your support in these final days. My name is Kurt Alme. I am a Montana native. I was born in Great Falls. My dad taught high school math. My mom was an elementary school teacher. Throughout my life, I’ve lived across the state from Dillon to Victor to Helena to Miles City. I’ve spent my entire career serving and protecting Montana families. As Montana’s Budget Director and Revenue Director, I spearheaded two of the largest tax cuts in state history, balanced our state budget, and helped make Montana debt-free. I’ll fight to do it again in Washington. As Montana’s U.S. Attorney, nominated by President Trump and confirmed by the Senate twice, we went after violent criminals, expanded drug prevention and treatment, and targeted drug traffickers all the way to the cartels – and tore them out by their roots. Last year my office prosecuted more criminals than any year in the last 20 years, and we drove down violent crime. **I am the only candidate in this race with deep Montana roots and a proven record of cutting taxes, balancing our state budget, and locking up violent criminals. I am not a career politician. I am stepping up to serve again because Montana is my home. I want our kids and grandkids to have an even better life than we have, with the same freedoms and values that we hold dear. President Trump has given this campaign his Complete and Total Endorsement. With less than two weeks left and votes already being cast, this race is in its final stretch. Folks, Texas Republicans do not trust you. And are afraid that Vikki Goodwin is about to flip the Lieutenant Governor’s office. We know this because **they've been caught planning to strip the office of its legislative power** and potentially violate the state constitution. **This would be a blatant disregard for the will of the people.
** As Vikki Goodwin’s campaign manager, I can tell you this is a credible rumor. Goodwin filed a police report, his team cited them as "parodies," while quickly taking them down. And every day, they keep lying about her stance on taxes and criminal justice. Republicans are counting on voters _not understanding_ that this is the most powerful elected position in Texas. Our campaign has been working hard to educate the public — and we've closed the gap. We have 11 days left. Let me explain what's at stake. |
---

Peter -

Here's a breakdown of our race ... _by the numbers_.

**$9 million:**
This is how much Annie Andrews raised last quarter.
I got into this race long after she was already raising millions of dollars from liberals all over the country. She has the support of Hollywood stars like Star Wars' Mark Hamill and Roseanne's John Goodman.

**3 months:**
How long I've been in this race.
I did not seek this moment, Peter. I never thought I'd be in this position. Politics was Lindsey's thing. But when President Trump asked me to run for a full Senate term, I knew I had to answer the call to, once again, serve the people of South Carolina.

Since entering, I am running my third statewide campaign in just three months. I know so many of you have been so generous to help me, but it's taken its toll. Our campaign is running on fumes.

**RCP Average: +2.7:**
**Darline Graham: 48%**
**Annie Andrews: 45.3%**
This is the average of all the recent polls in the South Carolina Senate races. We're only up by 2.7%.

Annie Andrews and her liberal Super PACs have spent millions attacking me, spreading lies about my family and me. She's also lying about where she stands on the issues. She's wearing a "moderate mask" that will disappear IF she's elected to the Senate to stand with Chuck Schumer, James Talarico, and Abdul El-Sayed.

**11 Days:**
_That's all we have left before Election Day._
Time isn't on our side, Peter. **[To finish out this race, I need you by my side.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=dd558ae24b5344759333940f5da8053c&_e=OMI3YKQY0qmoYpF3NzOPWiBps69fYTFAUwunYWLmxDIQq_ZpEXNdPr23iWyamL9cxjji9AsYIQ7oQfKIl-JUh_GPhuMMFW1G_EopylkEnLgKUmiUKi2Hn3vAc0z_zKgZN1eRKjzNvSWldbDOYo-ooI3cLKpXzKI3fmSthBmOomAvDEB8pONkzitDoAuNgg6XSoZ5wFj-F_p1sop87oNW4YjOCqACU6WsB-b8RljLxzONC5AS3SgSI9gQD4QLdAKjRqTE_ATAqejlSLhAu2qMsHPy08e6ZIFKg6MFmYbJmT1x10wfJOoDC1EoaWASLaUbY2T2zVtfNqvQdNEaihCMe-23EPRAj72EnJp9rXtVBzqRbMDa1F72vau2-2SSgGhzlN0ezo2GBadX1Jg0sV0PSeeoDbzYfcuAapbI27hoodvplvYrGT523__CEzo8E3m5U6j5voZtNPpqWW3L-6I-iGKspjibUIQVhX2Lyl3CSnDZMMNO0PsZRNj3DlZOhk7veV1KwD1WFRz8FGQbyqD023nNfmI2YLYpmlSBJ5rBLFuInk2ni89cAurKojdMtde0b6W1zDm-ptb1lhOTzZUrkO1y12bVTGRDvqSKa630gLS6ns64Hkvl41pVLTY_K_Wqcq93uopSdfhnv1LMFSdrgMA0fOBWWHU_7l4gkl7pmcqvH4lVAdoIxDUWEgaUp9-RR1dfr-2NbpLI8seqr-CzpMuLpj9TCuRNSQnVdx4gxwk%3D)**

I can't win this alone. I'm counting on grassroots conservatives like you, not big-money donors, to get us across the finish line. **[Will you chip in $10 or even $20 right now?](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=dd558ae24b5344759333940f5da8053c&_e=OMI3YKQY0qmoYpF3NzOPWiBps69fYTFAUwunYWLmxDIQq_ZpEXNdPr23iWyamL9cxjji9AsYIQ7oQfKIl-JUh_GPhuMMFW1G_EopylkEnLgKUmiUKi2Hn3vAc0z_zKgZN1eRKjzNvSWldbDOYo-ooI3cLKpXzKI3fmSthBmOomAvDEB8pONkzitDoAuNgg6XSoZ5wFj-F_p1sop87oNW4YjOCqACU6WsB-b8RljLxzONC5AS3SgSI9gQD4QLdAKj_hMAYGgwgRzIyDhsv9qs2LV8n6W-C4MuFXddSy39KJJDP18yf86I7eGRiYqiI_YUFHdPtXuJcUStjkgt_Q_6ST9ZiNa_13aYBXTU-NjB4WxyhznobZUwuwfhiHkRyzFgiHW9bu28LC-NYUXwcvkIkMtm_lJnTA8QIvW96crj1p2479vTGhjFAiJfY0S0axBM6fhUViCo7on0gIXZiLbJJ-9Wt1WVx-fOTwBXxbo3_EWAA-nT7ZvUXpIopbTTN9bqZsUYxbnE5e-rJfBIL-jlF257utHDLUf9bJ_wRUni_UhceHHtzHCSSV_H-aJI_4qLpOvT2e7YI9bChSafjfcd13141CzDf-7P1RFLf5VBuPtLS4-OUaMfGfZO9x9TflcIyEeSVfa5sYsfrDejINlOcg05HIyfswBrkUStyioTghl4fXzinfEx07UqAvC_VQMwArs0nZ39xoYDeSpgCiihNPr3jZe1-31Tm7b29WL1Mvc%3D)**

Federal law requires TV and radio stations to sell ad time to candidates at their LOWEST UNIT RATE in the final 60 days before a general election. That's the same rate the station gives its best commercial customer. Super PACs don't get that rate. They pay whatever the station charges. During a football game in Austin in September, a Republican super PAC was charged $450,000 to air a single ad. Talarico's campaign paid $50,000 for a spot in the same game, in the same market. That's NINE TIMES the price. So when Democrats send money straight to their candidates, every dollar buys MORE airtime than a super PAC dollar. And that's exactly what they're doing. For years, the Left has built a national small-dollar machine. Liberal donors don't just give to candidates at home. They give to candidates in states they've never visited. Talarico has raised more than $122 million from individual donors this cycle, and more than $65 million of it came from small donors giving $200 or less. If James Talarico wins in Texas, it will be because of that mountain of small-dollar contributions. Once your money moves away from the candidate's own campaign, it buys less. That's why the Senate Conservatives Fund makes it easy to give directly. You can support multiple candidates with a single, secure transaction. SCF pays all fundraising costs and transfers 100% of your candidate contributions to their campaigns. Please help these conservatives close the money gap today: U.S. Senate ✅ Ken Paxton (TX) ✅ Roger Marshall (KS) ✅ Mike Collins (GA) ✅ Ashley Moody (FL) U.S. House ✅ Scott Perry (PA-10) ✅ Joe Mitchell (IA-02) ✅ Nick Begich (AK-AL) ✅ Eli Crane (AZ-02) ✅ Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) ✅ Alex Mealer (TX-09) And if you give $100 or more by October 31, one of our top supporters — Mike Rydin from Houston — has agreed to donate $100 to multiply your contribution. Election Day is November 3. There's no time to waste. Tesla’s Driverless Miles Grew Eightfold in a Single Quarter. The Car With No Steering Wheel Is Already Giving Rides.
On October 21, Tesla reported that its robotaxis had logged nearly 2 million unsupervised miles, eight times more than three months earlier. Its Cybercab, built with no steering wheel or pedals, started carrying riders in Austin on September 3. Most people still think this is a decade away.
Threat level 3/5 — Guarded

---
For most of your life, self-driving cars were always “ten years away.” Every year, the date moved. That’s why so many people stopped paying attention. But the numbers Tesla reported this week show something different: the miles aren’t growing gradually anymore. They’re multiplying.
The evidence board
| | What Tesla Just Reported
---|---
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit A — the miles.** Cumulative unsupervised robotaxi miles grew eightfold in the third quarter to nearly 2 million, according to Tesla’s Q3 results.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit B — the vehicle.** The Cybercab began giving robotaxi rides in Austin on September 3. Tesla says installed Cybercab capacity in Texas is now more than 125,000 units a year.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit C — the customers.** Active subscriptions to Tesla’s supervised self-driving software grew 67% from a year earlier to 1.74 million.
| EVIDENCE
---
**Exhibit D — the cost of driving.** Gasoline averaged $4.33 a gallon nationally in September, a record for the month, and above $6 in California.
| OUR THEORY
---
Every driverless car is really a computer on wheels. It has to see, process and decide in real time, with no human backup. The companies that make that possible get paid on every vehicle, whichever robotaxi company wins.

Medical workers treat injured people at Ameth Bek hospital after a drone strike on a market in the disputed Abyei region along the border between South Sudan and Sudan, October 19, 2026. REUTERS/Medecins Sans Frontieres/Handout via REUTERS.
Mubarak Musa Adam, a 44-year-old trader, had already left Al-Na'am, a market known locally as Amiet Common Market in Abyei town, the administrative center of the disputed oil-rich region between Sudan and South Sudan, on October 19 when he made the fateful decision to turn back.
"He had prepared his Land Cruiser, loaded it with fuel and goods, and they left the market," his cousin, Al-Shafie Abdullah, 42, told Drop Site News. "But then he remembered that he still had to pay the rest of what he owed to a Somali trader he worked with in the fuel business. He went back with our cousin to the trader's shop, and as soon as they got there, the market was hit by a drone."
Adam was killed in the attack along with another cousin, Al-Fatih Daoud Adam, the Somali trader, and two of the trader's brothers. The strikes, which occurred at approximately noon local time, killed at least 152 people and wounded 47, Murtada Ahmed, spokesperson for the Kordofan Observatory, a field monitoring and human rights group, told Drop Site. Ahmed blamed the attack on the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF).
The same toll was confirmed by Saif al-Din David, director of the Free Pens Human Rights Observatory, which also operates in the Kordovan region. He added that the strikes also burned around 500 shops. ACLED, an organization that monitors violence, put the toll even higher, at between 150 and 220 people and displacing around 8,000.
"Initial findings indicate that a military aircraft deployed an estimated 22 munitions directly into a heavily populated commercial area demonstrating a flagrant disregard for human life and international legal norms," the Abyei Special Administrative Area (ABAA) said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/ef577efe-f360-46e7-b961-cb48a0059645?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that also blamed the SAF.
Adam was one of many traders from Nyala, in South Darfur, who worked the route south to the border. "They carried onions and some local products to al-Na'am, and brought back food and fuel to Nyala, Ed Daein, El Geneina, Zalingei, and other localities," Al-Shafie said. "To me, that moment sums up Mubarak's honesty and decency," Al-Shafie added. "He made sure to give people what they were owed before he left this life."
Al-Shafie was elsewhere at the time of the attack. "Most of the survivors were people who were outside the market when the attack happened, and I was one of them," he said. "I had malaria and went for tests at the hospital in Abyei. When we came back, we found the bodies of the victims burned and charred: Somalis, Sudanese from the north and from the south, and people from the Dinka and Misseriya, the two communities who share this area."
## **Targeting a Vital Crossing**
Abyei is a disputed region between Sudan and South Sudan, and its administrative and political status remains contested. The market at Al-Na'am sits in a demilitarized zone that has been administered and monitored by the United Nations Interim Security Force for Abyei ([UNISFA](https://substack.com/redirect/214cd711-a0e2-4991-913d-b389232c742e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)) since its formation in June 2011.
"Al-Na'am is one of the vital trade crossings that supply Darfur and Kordofan with food, medicine, fuel, and other basic needs. It is a lifeline for western Sudan," Murtada Ahmed, spokesperson for the Kordofan Observatory, a field monitoring and human rights group, said. "Targeting it with drones threatens to cut that lifeline and besiege the people of Kordofan with hunger and disease."
Darfur and Kordofan are under the control of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), the paramilitary group led by General Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, that has been locked in a brutal conflict for the past three and a half years with the SAF, led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. The war erupted in April 2023 when a long simmering rivalry between the two factions exploded into fighting four years after protesters toppled longtime president Omar al-Bashir following a 2019 popular uprising.
At least 150,000 people have been killed, with some estimates running far higher. Some 14 million have been forced from their homes, more than 4.5 million of them across Sudan's borders, and the International Rescue Committee says more people face famine in Sudan than in the rest of the world combined.
The RSF and its allies, now organized in the Sudan Founding Alliance with the Sudan People's Liberation Movement-North and Darfuri armed groups, hold Darfur and large parts of Kordofan, the regions that depend on the border trade. The SAF, whose government is based in Port Sudan, is pushing back into Kordofan, recently capturing towns such as al-Mazroub.
The RSF has been accused in some of the worst atrocities of the conflict, with a UN fact-finding mission [concluding](https://substack.com/redirect/30eba9b8-c244-4922-934f-fdd980e8fe52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) earlier this year that the RSF takeover of El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, in October 2025 "bore the hallmarks of genocide."
However, the SAF has also committed atrocities of its own, and the UN has found it [responsible](https://substack.com/redirect/eadff6b6-bbaa-471c-bf65-cd51c0f08207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for direct and large-scale attacks against civilians and other war crimes.
For the past two weeks, the SAF has been conducting a large-scale aerial operation--launching near-daily attacks on RSF-controlled cities in Darfur, Kordofan, and other parts of Sudan--that has killed scores of civilians.
"Although the attack is the first round of drone strikes recorded at Amieth Market since the Sudan war began in April 2023, ACLED data shows that it was not the first instance of political violence at the site during the conflict," Kelvin Karingithi, South Sudan Analyst at ACLED told Drop Site.
"The region continues to experience intercommunal clashes, mainly involving the local Ngok Dinka and Misseriya communities, with the most recent incidents occurring in and around Amieth Market on September 15 and 16, resulting in at least 40 killed and over 100 injuries," he added.
The majority Ngok Dinka population has historically favored joining South Sudan, while the seasonal Misseriya pastoralists from Sudan, who are backed by the RSF, have not. The members of the Ngok Dinka and Misseriya communities agreed to reopen the Amiet joint border market on September 28, following its closure due to the two-day clash in mid-September.
"The rivalry between the two communities centers largely on land, grazing, and resources, as well as broader political issues. South Sudan plans to include Abyei in its first elections since independence scheduled for December 22, 2026, despite Sudan's opposition and the area's unresolved status," Karingithi explained.

On October 18, the day before the strike on Al-Na'am market, a drone strike blamed on the SAF hit al-Debab, a town in RSF-controlled West Kordofan, south of Mujlad city. The strike hit a truck stop beside the market, where people gathered at the end of the market day to board trucks and private vehicles back to their villages.
The Sudan Founding Alliance, a political coalition headed by the RSF, described the attack that killed scores of people as a double-tap strike. "The drone first struck a gathering of people preparing to board a truck after attending a funeral gathering. It then waited for others to arrive to help the wounded and struck a second time. The double-tap attack killed 80 people and wounded many more, including children, women and men," the coalition's spokesperson Ahmed Tagad Lisan said in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/55a1ecd1-b91a-40fe-831b-4de5bcac85e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
The same drone also fired a missile at the town of al-Muglad, which landed near a girls' school and wounded at least two people, he added.
The death toll in the attack on Al-Debab increased to 120 three days later as dozens of critically wounded victims succumbed to their injuries, according to David of the Free Pens Human Rights Observatory, who noted that SAF drone strikes occur almost daily in the region.
Another drone strike in West Kordofan, also attributed to the SAF by the Kordovan Observatory, killed four people of the same family when their truck was hit on a road linking Abu Qalb, in Abu Zabad locality, and Al-Mazroub, a town the army recently captured.

His maternal aunt, Hajja Maryam Ali, 82, was sick and could not find treatment near home, so the family set out from Abu Qalb to Al-Mazroub. "The drone hit the vehicle while it was moving," Kuku told Drop Site. His aunt, Maryam, was killed with her daughters, Um Khamisa Ali, 48, and Al-Tomah Ali, 46, along with her grandson, Fadl al-Sayed, 27. Two of the four other passengers were wounded.
"Fadl was a groom about to be married. His wedding was set for December," Kuku said. "They were a simple family: two sisters who went with their mother and her grandson, and they were all killed together."
The truck, a Nissan cargo vehicle known locally as a "lorry," belonged to Al-Tomah's husband, Habiballah Mohamed Ali, who is now left with their two sons, Mohamed, 16, and Ahmed, 8.
"In the first two years of the war we could still farm, but in the last two years the front lines reached us, and the drones fly over civilians' heads day and night," Kuku said. "The family went out looking for treatment and survival, and the journey ended with all of them dead."

body:
Courts are standing against Trump’s illegal and chaotic attempts to hijack the 2026 midterm elections.
| | | | | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_G7RHp35-QEwRqRqcgIrEghfHO1FcMAlju-ZikDkXFRCat8evo9s_IG3s5hINZZT3JbWXqOBWW1OCjjGYteWpeEEtk1S3quYeu3dRa2THaP77MDm88TATB4LHIrg71036D9xdpEl2qp7i5709PIAdsF1dklK8l1qbhjZQsADu2LTzw7S1zEuHW-MHWToxTY9VAaF_4TFGs60eR_46whX6TQs9_bpW3C0XwnXHTE--v0=&c=FuRkVnNe8d1MazFqgK36tcTmun_wIFOtZpsof-TtS7t9YQL7flmFXA==&ch=ZvDLX4QHjFez9BLqlC-EK21B2w6y7QK1rMLUHdbeiIcadrQwZdl5_g==)
---
|
Peter,
A federal judge just ruled against the Department of Homeland Security's attempts to conduct unjustified stops and door to door sweeps as part of Trump's bogus "Unlawful Voter Initiative."
The "Surge" as they referred to it internally at DHS relied on "error-prone government lists" that were shown to be sweeping U.S. citizens into the DHS dragnet -- putting at risk thousands of valid voters in the Trump Admin's quixotic quest to find voter fraud committed by non-citizens.
Now it isn't just ICE conducting raids and questioning anyone who looks "foreign": DHS' "Homeland Security Investigations" is taking the lead, the very same branch of the agency that conducted the raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar.
---
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001_G7RHp35-QEwRqRqcgIrEghfHO1FcMAlju-ZikDkXFRCat8evo9s_IG3s5hINZZT3JbWXqOBWW1OCjjGYteWpeEEtk1S3quYeu3dRa2THaP77MDm88TATB4LHIrg71036D9xdpEl2qp7i5709PIAdsF1dklK8l1qbhjZQsADu2LTzw7S1zEuHW-MHWToxTY9VAaF_4TFGs60eR_46whX6eC_Is0xM_liYdTSwFg73v4=&c=FuRkVnNe8d1MazFqgK36tcTmun_wIFOtZpsof-TtS7t9YQL7flmFXA==&ch=ZvDLX4QHjFez9BLqlC-EK21B2w6y7QK1rMLUHdbeiIcadrQwZdl5_g==)
---
Homeland Security has no business interfering in state-run elections. It has no business interrogating Americans at their doors without probable cause or due legal process.
Sen. Mark Kelly (D-Arizona) called this out as voter intimidation and urged citizens to not be deterred, to make sure their votes are cast and counted.
We agree. But our work is more crucial now than ever: and Defend Our Courts' Emergency GOTV funds are already being used to help any voters who sent mail-in ballots disenfranchised in North Carolina--way ahead of schedule and completely unexpected this early in the voting.

Everyone knows June is Pride Month — a time to celebrate queer joy, visability and the community that makes us who we are. **But October is LGBT History month,** _and I can’t stop thinking about the historic giants whose work made it possible for so many of us to live and serve our communities openly._ [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142052211/655632227/1120685057?refcode=RS_EM_EN_2026.10.23_LGBTHistory&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDIvMS82NzI5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNmQxODRmMC0xZGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1Uw7uxilQjHSKZ4AiMi-khvp333fD6If6znib-IWY9A=) When I first ran for Congress, the possibility that my candidacy could offer people in my district a kind of visibility and representation they hadn’t seen before was central to my campaign. I feel incredibly lucky to now serve as the first queer Latina elected to Congress. But I didn’t get here alone. I’m standing on the shoulders of generations of queer people who fought for the chance for someone like me to run, win, and serve openly. October is about remembering the people who refused to disappear: the activists who fought for their communities, the artists and athletes who gave us a glimpse of ourselves, and the everyday people who lived openly when doing so took real courage. The attacks on queer people we’re witnessing today aren’t new. And neither is our community's resilience. We’ve got to remember that, especially as we watch real attempts to erase transgender people from public life and roll back the rights our community fought so hard to win. We know better than to disappear. We know better than to let our history be erased. And we’re not going anywhere. Thank you for fighting with me for visibility, freedom, and a future where every queer kid can see a place for themselves in the story. — Emily 💙 | | Emily Randall is proud to represent Washington’s 6th District in Congress. She grew up in a working-class Union household in Port Orchard and was the first in her family to attend college. After serving in the State Senate and passing nearly 200 bills, Emily made history in 2024 as the first queer Latina elected to Congress. body:
Nearly one-third of those voters in Georgia are under the age of 30.
#
Peter,
Early voting in Georgia is happening right now, and turnout is already surging —**more than 1 million ballots have officially been cast in this critical election.**
Georgia's political landscape has transformed, and our community is at the very heart of that change.
The state’s Latino electorate has climbed to over 400,000 registered voters, making up more than 4% of the statewide total. Even more remarkable — nearly one-third of those voters are under the age of 30.
In a battleground where recent elections have come down to razor-thin margins, Latino voters hold the decisive power to defend Jon Ossoff’s U.S. Senate seat and elect Keisha Lance Bottoms as Georgia's next governor.
The potential is undeniable. But potential alone doesn't win elections — _turnout does._
Right now, Voto Latino is working around the clock to contact, inform, and mobilize hundreds of thousands of young and newly registered Latino voters across Georgia before the polls close.

| |

Hi there, It's Morghan, Nellie's campaign manager. I want to fill you in on something that doesn't come up much in campaign emails but shapes almost every decision I make this time of year: cash flow. Most people think about campaign fundraising in terms of totals, but in the final stretch of a race, the question I'm asking every morning is different. It's not just how much we have. But also when we have it. Ad time has to be reserved and paid for ahead of when it airs, our field program runs on a schedule, and get-out-the-vote plans get locked in days in advance. In other words, a dollar that comes in today can do far more than a dollar that comes in the night before the election. Today, it can become an ad, a door knock, or a phone call. On November 2nd, there's very little left that it can still buy. **[That's why I'm asking you to give now, while your contribution can still go to work in every part of our closing plan. clean_body: This shapes almost every decision I make | | Hi there, It's Morghan, Nellie's campaign manager. I want to fill you in on something that doesn't come up much in campaign emails but shapes almost every decision I make this time of year: cash flow. Most people think about campaign fundraising in terms of totals, but in the final stretch of a race, the question I'm asking every morning is different. It's not just how much we have. But also when we have it. Ad time has to be reserved and paid for ahead of when it airs, our field program runs on a schedule, and get-out-the-vote plans get locked in days in advance. In other words, a dollar that comes in today can do far more than a dollar that comes in the night before the election. Today, it can become an ad, a door knock, or a phone call. Members are still allowed to buy and sell individual stocks while they’re voting on the laws that move those very markets. **I PROUDLY support a comprehensive ban on congressional stock trading. Period.** And since I’m asking you to hold Congress to that standard, you should know I don’t buy or sell individual stocks, and I never will while I’m serving you. Friends,
I’ve said it on the trail and I’ll say it again: South Dakota’s next governor should answer to South Dakotans.

Over just two days this week, Gov. Rhoden’s campaign reported **$135,000 from a single political action committee based in Clayton, Missouri**. The same federal PAC has been one of the largest funders of his campaign all year. Take a look at his own filing:
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| |

Here’s what our campaign looks like. **The vast majority of our contributions come from individuals, and almost all come from right here in South Dakota.** Our donors are teachers in Aberdeen, ranchers west of the river, and small business owners from Sioux Falls to Rapid City. They give $10, $25, or $50 because they want a governor who works for them.
That’s the choice in this race. One campaign is being propped up by out-of-state PAC money. The other is being built by the people who live here.
South Dakota will not be astroturfed. We deserve better than a governor bought and paid for from somewhere else.
You may have seen the polls that have us down. Here’s what I’d remind you about that same pollster. Last year, surveys had Dusty Johnson leading the Republican primary for governor, with Toby Doeden at 4%. Then voters actually voted. Doeden finished first, and Dusty didn’t even make the runoff.
Polls don’t decide elections._**You do.**_ And the people who know this race best are already moving our way: a majority of independents are with us.
_**Our biggest challenge isn’t persuasion. It’s making sure every South Dakotan knows who we are before November 3, and that takes resources.**_
We have 11 days until Election Day, and we’re close to the fundraising goal that funds our full plan for the final stretch. **Whether you can give $10 or more, your support will help us cross the finish line.** Every dollar you give is a South Dakota dollar, and that’s what makes this campaign different.
Let’s go win,Dan Ahlers _Your Candidate For Governor_

Hey folks,
Elon Musk suddenly has regrets.
After spending enormous amounts of money helping elect Donald Trump and putting himself at the center of DOGE, Musk now says he got "carried away" and should've stayed in the background. With the midterms two weeks away and Democrats threatening investigations, the timing is pretty damn interesting.
* [**00:01:23**] Elon Musk admits he should've stayed in the background, and reflects on getting a little too intoxicated by his access to Trump and the Oval Office.
* [**00:04:41**] Democrats are promising investigations into Musk and his businesses if they retake Congress, and Musk is already threatening retaliation.
* [**00:06:08**] Musk lashes out at Kara Swisher after she raises questions about investigations involving him, while new scrutiny emerges over his reported role restricting Ukraine's access to Starlink.
* [**00:08:41**] It's not just Musk: Peter Thiel and other tech billionaires suddenly seem much more willing to distance themselves from Trump as the political winds start shifting.
* [**00:11:43**] Musk reportedly wants to combine Tesla and SpaceX in a massive deal before Trump leaves office, and I explain why Democrats need to fight it instead of letting billionaire power grow even stronger.

This is bigger than Elon Musk. It's about billionaires using their money and access to shape our government, and then repositioning themselves the second they think power might change hands. Democrats cannot let themselves be bought off when these people come knocking. We can take on oligarchs, we can demand accountability, and we can build a government that works for ordinary people again. **If you value independent media willing to challenge concentrated power, help me keep fighting.**

body:
| | | Hi there, it's Martin Sheen. I know seeing my name in your inbox might come as a surprise, but I need to talk to you about the country we both love ‐‐ and why I hope you'll fight for it alongside me.

If you don't have time to hear my whole pitch, here's my ask: [**Will you join me in the fight for our future by donating $7 _(generously matched to $21)_ to help my friends at the DSCC take back the Senate for Democrats?**](https://go.dscc.org/go/24462?amount=7&t=5&firstname=&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&addr1=&addr2=&city=Cresco&state=Pennsylvania&zip=18326&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&ask=7&amounts=7%2C14%2C28%2C70&code=DPE-FD-20261023-MartinSheen-WhatASKMeans2026RF-Pros-sl1&refcode=DPE-FD-20261023-MartinSheen-WhatASKMeans2026RF-Pros-sl1&akid=27033%2E9716520%2EKVPB9u)

**Good Afternoon!** Today's special sponsor and investment opportunity comes from [Miso Robotics](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A), which is helping revolutionize the restaurant industry with its innovative Flippy robot, bringing automation and advanced technology to some of America's biggest restaurant brands. Now, with its latest 3D-vision technology on the horizon, [Miso is offering investors a limited-time opportunity](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A) to own a stake in its future before its current investment campaign closes tomorrow night. -- Cole, CEO

A recent robotics IPO was oversubscribed 8,000X, and nuts and bolts flew in celebration. Experts say the frenzy could reprice robotics stocks everywhere. Meanwhile, everyday investors like you didn't miss an opportunity to get in on this boom with over 44,000 investments in [a private-stage company named Miso Robotics.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A) But Miso's "$1.3 with Vision 3D" campaign ends at midnight. Miso's Flippy robot works the fry station and was already boosting profits up to 4x for restaurant brands like White Castle. That led [industry powerhouse Ecolab to invest in Miso's growth and NVIDIA to collaborate.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A) After [Miso made two major asset acquisitions in 2026](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A), Flippy is the star of Miso's expanding ecosystem. Customers think of it as the new operating system for modern restaurants. This year alone, Miso added big-name customers like Jersey Mike's and Cinnabon, and grew its patent portfolio by ~10X to over 300. Its robots have even expanded beyond restaurants, entering [college campuses and NBA arenas.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyskEHO2yAQhU-Dd7ZgIOAsWFSKsku3XSIM43gqYyzASXv7ylFV9QD_dr5P857ej4d7eFppe373CW2bs4sYKfiG0W34riu2hsX5beSc_8ovLPWYaig0YaT9fxs46F7wHqQTXbQzIqDs0ApzBTNelYZusUJADEIZKf2IFy3CKIwHbkZuYtB-6siefwQHCYIrEINCf0WYZUAPGjUyxTFSy2X4mWlrC87r77PWEHLqVru0tlcmvzG4M7jT9sLahkQ1lzzlRqGe3gnl_WjJ1XyUgEzeMHlaGejzmDDSkZi87Z5iv_vSNix1of0vDz7tnp7bx_gHxch7BcadE4CTUoz8oi6C867YuL9pXalqwxR_nlGfuu3rBn9Z-BMAAP__0W6Y8A) Now, Miso's introducing new NVIDIA 3D-vision tech. name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: This is my message for you, Peter.
body:
Here's why I'm writing to you specifically:
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, this isn't one of our usual campaign updates. I know you hear from my team often, so I wanted to write to you myself today because we've hit a moment in this race that I don't think anyone saw coming a year ago.
**In the last month,_six_ _separate polls_ have shown me leading Greg Abbott in the race for Governor.**
Abbott had never been shown trailing in a public poll before last month — in any race he’s ever run. In twelve years and three campaigns for governor, Abbott has never faced anything like this.
But here's what worries me: **Tomorrow night is our final public fundraising deadline before the election.**
_**This is the moment when your support in this race matters most, Peter.**_
**That’s why we set a goal to raise $7 million before the October 24th TEC fundraising deadline. This is the minimum amount of money we need to raise, and falling short is not an option. As of writing this email, we’re 94.58% of the way there.**
According to our records, you haven't had the chance to chip in yet this month, and I wanted to make sure you heard about where we stand from me before the deadline passes.
Here's what I want you to understand about timing: This race is a real toss-up, and the window where your grassroots donation can help us hold onto our lead is _right now._
[**Will you make your first contribution of the month right now, even just $5, and help us raise the $7,000,000 we urgently need by tomorrow at midnight?**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_3_message.Km9BpW&refcode=em20261023-2518&amount=5&t=2&akid=2518%2E299639%2EN9wS8x)
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261023_3_message.Km9BpW&amount=5&refcode=em20261023-2518&t=21&akid=2518%2E299639%2EN9wS8x)
Thank you,
Gina
_Our records aren’t perfect – if you’ve donated with a different email address, phone number, or by check, not all of your gifts may be reflected in our accounting here. Our team greatly appreciates all of your support in electing me as the next Governor of Texas!_

Peter, it’s Mary Peltola. I want you to hear this from me:
The Trump Administration is suing preemptively to try to keep Dan Sullivan in power because they're terrified he’ll lose this race in 11 days.

clean_body: DC people want to play partisan games while I am fighting for Alaska’s future. | = Peter, it's Mary Peltola. I want you to hear this from me: The Trump Administration is suing preemptively to try to keep Dan Sullivan in power because they're terrified he’ll lose this race in 11 days. = | = Look, Peter, I'm not used to this Lower 48 hyperpartisan BS. It's not how we do things in Alaska. Where I'm from, in the Bush, there's a big premium on respect. We depend on each other too much to burn bridges over political differences. But if they think I won't fight back when D.C. people try to play partisan games with our future, they've got another thing coming. I'm running to take on the rigged D.C. system that's hurting all of us, and I won't let this sham stop me. But the truth is, the only way we're going to make sure every single Alaskan's voice is heard over the next 11 days is together. That's why I need all hands on deck right now to respond. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue, your donation will go through immediately: = | = ---|--- I'm the underdog in this battle against the D.C. establishment, so I'm counting on a huge grassroots effort to fight back in this final stretch. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142056018/655644545/-185804088?refcode=em-10.23.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjAyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMWYyM2RmYy0yOGNmLWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDIyNDgyOWY4NjkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=dnRZvvZntpzFU_G3Zln3734nJnWlveWflf_Z54WGFbc=) Friend, Tomorrow, early voting starts in Michigan. This weekend is also our second-to-last weekend of voter outreach before Election Day. With both of those coming up at once, I wanted to take a minute to write you something a little longer than usual. When this campaign started, a lot of people told us this would be one of the hardest re-election fights in the country. They were right. Outside groups started spending millions against us from the very beginning. We knew there wasn’t a shortcut. The only plan that made sense was to talk to as many people across this district as we possibly could and to keep doing it until the very last day. **So that’s what we did. ** From town halls and union halls to diners and front porches in Flint, Saginaw, and Bay City, I’ve spent the last two years hearing from folks and then getting to work for them – even when that meant taking on Elon Musk and special interests. This year, our team’s been out there too, knocking doors and picking up the phone. Most of those conversations haven’t been about politics. They’ve been about the cost of groceries, kids who have moved away to find work, and parents trying to afford their prescriptions. Those are the things I take to the Capitol with me. My opponent went to the Capitol on January 6. On November 3, voters here will decide which of us they want representing them. The days ahead will decide whether all of our work adds up to a win, and this final stretch is the most expensive part of any campaign: the ads, the mail, and the reminders that get people to the polls. clean_body: | = Friend, Tomorrow, early voting starts in Michigan. This weekend is also our second-to-last weekend of voter outreach before Election Day. With both of those coming up at once, I wanted to take a minute to write you something a little longer than usual. When this campaign started, a lot of people told us this would be one of the hardest re-election fights in the country. They were right. Outside groups started spending millions against us from the very beginning. We knew there wasn’t a shortcut. The only plan that made sense was to talk to as many people across this district as we possibly could and to keep doing it until the very last day. So that’s what we did. From town halls and union halls to diners and front porches in Flint, Saginaw, and Bay City, I’ve spent the last two years hearing from folks and then getting to work for them – even when that meant taking on Elon Musk and special interests. This year, our team’s been out there too, knocking doors and picking up the phone. Most of those conversations haven’t been about politics. They’ve been about the cost of groceries, kids who have moved away to find work, and parents trying to afford their prescriptions. Those are the things I take to the Capitol with me. My opponent went to the Capitol on January 6. On November 3, voters here will decide which of us they want representing them. The days ahead will decide whether all of our work adds up to a win, and this final stretch is the most expensive part of any campaign: the ads, the mail, and the reminders that get people to the polls. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thank you, KMR | We'd hate to see you go, but you can click here if you'd like to . Friend,

I don’t usually say this out loud, but I’m nervous.

**Everywhere I go, I keep hearing the same thing:** _“North Carolina is gone.” “We’re going to lose it.” “And if we lose North Carolina, we lose the Majority.”_

I refuse to believe that. But I’d be lying if I told you it hasn’t been keeping me up at night.

body:

---
Derek, this is an email from the Democratic National Committee about our work to flip Congress in 10 days. If you need help checking your voter registration or making a plan to vote, please visit [iwillvote.com](https://ak.democrats.org/go/9784?t=2&akid=10083%2E22930333%2EaSBBJt). Democrats are getting _**absolutely hammered_** right now. _Hundreds of millions of dollars from Donald Trump and MAGA super PACs.
$276 million donated by Elon Musk to preserve the MAGA majority since July.
An onslaught of ads attacking Democrats on the airwaves._ **[Chip in $7 to fight back](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-october-2026-gfr.GS9qR7&amount=7&refcode=em_20261023_10021_fr&t=6&akid=10083%2E22930333%2EaSBBJt)** Derek, Republicans _know_ that losing control of Congress means the end of an unchecked Trump administration — and they’re _terrified._ That’s why they’re pummeling Democratic candidates in key battleground races with attack ads. But the honest truth is that it’s hard for our grassroots movement to keep up with a billionaire-backed machine. ### [Lewiston's Clerk Sets the Record Straight, Then Hands Out the Rules](https://substack.com/redirect/0bbad9eb-9af6-4a9b-9edd-66b97625519b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you or someone you know needs help at the booth in Lewiston, the rules for that help are now on paper. First, a correction to yesterday's lead. Citing a single unnamed source, we told you the clerk had escorted a translator out of Lewiston City Hall for electioneering. On Thursday the clerk said she had not asked the two translators to leave the polling area, and I deleted my post about it ([my clarification](https://substack.com/redirect/c4ca16af-72e8-4ac6-9a47-e327b4edb3b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). Later in the afternoon, City Clerk Kathy Montejo came outside to give Jon a fuller account. It was a warden, not the clerk, who told an interpreter to leave the voting area after the interpreter approached a newly arrived voter who hadn't asked for help. In Jon's words, "it wasn't a contentious exit." Whether anyone was told to leave the building is still unclear. Jon says an interpreter who got loud with him Wednesday may have been told to go, but he didn't see it himself.
The clerk is now handing out a sheet on what an "Aide" can and can't do. The voter has to ask for the aide, not the other way around. The aide has to read the entire ballot out loud and can't tell the voter how to vote. The voter marks the ballot and puts it in the envelope unless they're unable to. One aide per voter, and when they're done, the aide leaves the voting area with the voter. Mayor Carl Sheline, meanwhile, shared the city's new notice: no photos or video within 15 feet of a voter anywhere on City Hall's first floor, voter selfies excepted. He asked people to report voter harassment to the clerk. In other words, after the Maine Wire's photos of Somali "interpreters" breaking the law went viral, Sheline banned... photos. (This is the same Sheline who spent $40,000 of his own money to get a mayoral job that pays $7,000 per year.)
Then came the illegal electioneering.
Lewiston City Councilor Bret Martel, the Republican running in House District 95, told MWTV that 12 to 20 people, organized by the Maine People's Alliance from what he was told, came into the hallway outside the early voting room holding issue signs. Photographs show Democratic State Rep. Scott Harriman was among them. Martel says complaints had already forced him to take off a plain paper name tag and to pull the campaign magnets off his truck. Electioneering within 250 feet of a polling place is a Class E misdemeanor, and Martel says the clerk, after checking with the Attorney General's office, is treating early voting like Election Day.
No word yet on whether the Maine Republican Party is going to do anything about the scene in Lewiston, but the Republican National Committee has posted a tweet.
That'll show 'em!

### [$130 Million Refund to Maine Customers in Limbo as Electric Utilities Appeal Order to Cut Profits](https://substack.com/redirect/a21a07ff-78f3-46a1-ad78-b01480bf4284?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If you pay a CMP or Versant bill, roughly $130 million that federal regulators say belongs to Maine customers is stuck while the utilities fight it. In March, the regulators reaffirmed that New England's transmission owners had been allowed too much profit, cut their return on equity from 11.14% to 9.57%, and ordered more than $1.5 billion refunded by May 2027. Public Advocate Heather Sanborn (D) puts Maine's share at roughly $20 a month for a year for the average household, pending better numbers from the companies. CMP and Versant appealed in June, and CMP and its affiliate Maine Electric Power Co. are also suing the state officials who asked regulators to kill a 0.5% profit "adder." The average CMP bill, for the record, went from $91 in October 2020 to $157 this month. Delger Erdenesanaa of The Maine Monitor has the story.
### [Lewiston Youth Connected with Multiple Past Shootings And Charged with Attempted Murder Arrested Again on Drug Trafficking Warrant](https://substack.com/redirect/07cc35c2-6175-4c0f-8c25-681bc5ddf066?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Lewiston teenager charged with attempted murder last October is back in custody. Police arrested the 17-year-old Thursday on a drug-trafficking warrant after a resident brought them evidence, and they say he had cocaine base and more than $2,000 in cash on him. The attempted-murder case ended when he was found incompetent to stand trial. He'd also been charged in shootings in March 2024, April 2024 and June 2025, and was released every time. Seamus Othot has the story.
### [Lewiston Man Sentenced to 15 Years in Prison for Attempting to Sex Traffic Minors](https://substack.com/redirect/dbd9cd6d-36b2-4366-8d5d-cf0939a77b8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
A Lewiston man who tried to pay people he believed were minors for sex will spend the next 15 years in federal prison. Judge Stacey Neumann sentenced Dahir Muktar, 33, on Tuesday, and added 15 years of supervised release after that. He was arrested in January 2025, and a jury convicted him in April. Seamus Othot has the story.
### [SCOTUS Blocks Trump Administration from Ending Gender-Affirming Care for Prisoners](https://substack.com/redirect/e8f680ab-d1ab-45fc-bc83-753d3fe2f985?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Federal prisons can't end gender-transition treatment for inmates yet. The Supreme Court issued a short, unsigned order Wednesday, with no reasoning, that leaves in place Judge Royce Lamberth's block on the Bureau of Prisons' new policy, which would end surgeries, taper hormones and drop accommodations like wigs and makeup. Justices Thomas and Alito would have let the policy take effect. The case covers about 1,000 federal prisoners. Closer to home, a women's group protested outside the Women's Center at Windham earlier this month. Three Republican lawmakers showed up. None of the invited Democrats did. Libby Palanza has the story.
### [Westbrook Fugitive Caught After Six Days of Evading Law Enforcement](https://substack.com/redirect/2f82df23-c026-415a-bd48-6d76c6954b3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The man police were hunting after reports of shots fired in Rumford on Oct. 14 is in custody. That report put part of Rumford under a shelter-in-place order, and callers suspected drug dealing at the apartment. Blake Lachance, 21, of Westbrook, reportedly slipped away before police could set up a perimeter. U.S. Marshals tracked him to Westbrook, and he was caught Tuesday after he allegedly tried to run from a house on foot. He's charged with aggravated assault, aggravated reckless conduct and criminal mischief. Seamus Othot has the story.
### [Chinese Firms That Cashed In On Stolen Google AI Secrets Have Roots In Sam Altman's Overseas Venture](https://substack.com/redirect/218f28e6-e72b-4997-9ad3-24cbefa03483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The State Department's newest China sanctions hit an investment firm that, according to Bloomberg and TechCrunch, grew out of the China program Sam Altman started at Y Combinator. On Monday, State sanctioned Beijing-based MiraclePlus and four related entities over their ties to Linwei Ding, the former Google engineer convicted of stealing the company's AI trade secrets. MiraclePlus invested about $700,000 in Ding's startup. It was formed by YC China's former team after Y Combinator shut that program down in 2019, and Y Combinator says it has no affiliation with MiraclePlus. Peter, [The Trump administration just announced](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142056535/655646036/-1958284418?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDMyMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2I3MjExYTEtMmNjZi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAyMjQ4MjlmODY5IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=XqD4av_BaMiMXMTEzwizVec7tSY21SUEXblTe-if_mY=&emci=777211a1-2ccf-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&emdi=7b7211a1-2ccf-f111-bf5b-00224829f869&ceid=9848080) their plans to preemptively reject the results of Alaska’s Senate election if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. **Let that sink in: They are telling us ahead of time they won’t accept a Democratic victory.** This is an extraordinary abuse of federal power. Before voters have even cast their ballots, Trump’s Justice Department is trying to give itself a path to block certification of an election. We knew this was coming. I’ve said from the beginning that Democrats would have to overperform in every race to make sure Republicans can’t interfere with the results when they don’t get the outcome they want. Farm Bureau, Main Street tour, and a dog named Fern| | | |
---
Peter,We are moving non-stop on the campaign trail, and I want to bring you along for the fun: **Main Street Tour** I’m traveling across the district to talk to voters where they don’t usually meet politicians: bars, diners, and in their communities. Politics has gotten too sanitized, with leaders often running scared from the people they’re trying to represent. We have a different model, and we’re living that every day on this campaign. We stopped at Fox 21 for a live on-air interview where I answered important questions about what’s facing the district.
---
| | |
---
| | | **Farm Bureau Forum** On Thursday, I was grateful to join a forum co-hosted by the Wisconsin Farm Bureau and Wisconsin Farmers Union and take their questions about how we can improve the outlook for farmers. My closing argument was this: Wisconsin has a vibrant industry with incredible talent, now we need the government to foster growth rather than complicate it with tariff’s and harmful policy’s that leave farmers on shaky ground.Sadly, on these important topics my opponent Michael Alfonso offered little more than consultant-approved platitudes. He missed another opportunity to really discuss this critical industry and how Congress can support farmers. Wisconsin farmers deserve a leader who understands their challenges and can go to Washington and fight for them.

**Our TV Ad is Live** We’re going on TV in Wausau! This would not have been possible without the generosity of thousands of supporters, so thank you for helping us raise the dough to get on TV. Our message is direct and simple:

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, more than
any policy question, more than anything about the campaign, the thing
people often ask me right now is some version of: “Are we going to be
okay?”

I’ve thought a lot about how to answer that honestly, because the easy
answer is yes. But the easy answer isn’t always worth much.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19846?t=1001&akid=753%2E245147%2EVdtT1H ]So here’s the truth: We’re going to be okay, if enough people decide to
make it okay, and it won’t be if they don’t. Elections in this
Commonwealth come down to how many people step up in the last two weeks,
and we have exactly eleven of those days left. But everything in those
days takes serious resources, so please, will you chip in $25 today and be
part of the answer?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19847?t=1002&akid=753%2E245147%2EVdtT1H ]Donate →

What “making it okay” looks like, concretely, is
unglamorous, Derek.

It’s a volunteer in Allegheny County knocking her 40th door of the
afternoon. It’s a phone bank reaching people who’ve never been called
about a Governor’s race in their lives. It’s a thirty-second ad running
during a Thursday night broadcast in Johnstown because that’s where the
undecided voters actually are. None of it is dramatic, and all of it has
an invoice attached.

That’s the part people don’t see when they ask whether we’re going to be
okay. The answer isn’t in the polling. It’s whether there’s enough in the
bank account on October 24th to win on November 3rd.

And I understand why people are asking. It’s been a long few years, and a
lot is coming at folks at once. But Pennsylvania is one of the few places
left where the answer to that question — are we going to be okay? — is
genuinely up to the people being asked.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/19848?t=1003&akid=753%2E245147%2EVdtT1H ]So please,
Derek: If you want the answer
to that question to be yes, help make it yes. Chip in $25 or whatever you
can today — because Donald Trump’s allies are spending whatever it takes
to flip this must-win Governor’s office — and we can’t afford to slow
down.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

They sent Trump to Alaska. They sent Vance twice. Republican Senate leadership committed $17 MILLION. And Mary Peltola — a Yup'ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress — is still leading the race that decides the Senate majority. **So now they're asking a federal judge to deliver what their money couldn't.** First: election-law experts are already saying the case is baseless — no statute lets the DOJ block a state from certifying its own election, and one leading scholar expects it to be dismissed within weeks. It leans on a ballot dispute that Alaska's own Supreme Court already settled. Second: the markets watching this race didn't even flinch — Mary's standing held firm the day the suit dropped. clean_body: A lawsuit to stop certification before a single vote is counted A lawsuit to stop certification before a single vote is counted | ~~ | | We need you to understand exactly what just happened, because nothing like it has happened in a modern Senate race. Donald Trump's Justice Department filed a lawsuit in federal court asking a judge to block Alaska from certifying the results of its Senate election — if Mary Peltola wins. Read that again. Not a recount. Not a post-election challenge. A preemptive lawsuit, filed 11 days before Election Day, to stop a Peltola victory from ever being certified. Trump says he ordered it himself. They sent Trump to Alaska. They sent Vance twice. Republican Senate leadership committed $17 MILLION. And Mary Peltola — a Yup'ik leader and the first Alaska Native ever elected to Congress — is still leading the race that decides the Senate majority. So now they're asking a federal judge to deliver what their money couldn't. First: election-law experts are already saying the case is baseless — no statute lets the DOJ block a state from certifying its own election, and one leading scholar expects it to be dismissed within weeks. It leans on a ballot dispute that Alaska's own Supreme Court already settled. Second: the markets watching this race didn't even flinch — Mary's standing held firm the day the suit dropped. But "baseless" isn't the point, and they know it. The point is to muddy the final stretch, make Alaskans wonder whether their votes will count, and force Mary's campaign to fight in a courtroom while the election is won at the doors. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ Thank you. — Indigenous Women Lead | Paid for by Indigenous Women Lead PAC Indigenous Women Lead PACPO Box 15845Washington, DC 20003United States

The United States Army’s announcement on Tuesday that Fort Rucker will serve as its Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Autonomy Center of Excellence marks a major milestone for our military, for Enterprise, and for southeast Alabama. This new designation is a recognition of Fort Rucker’s role in the future of Army Aviation and an opportunity for our region to be part of the development, training, and innovation that will help shape that future. The effort was spearheaded by Enterprise native Katie Britt, who started this project when she served as Chief of Staff to Sen. Richard Shelby and finished it as the U.S. Senator for Alabama with Tuesday’s announcement.

U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, on Tuesday celebrated President Donald Trump’s signing of the Clergy Act, legislation she ushered unanimously through the Senate alongside Senator Maggie Hassan, D-New Hampshire, earlier this month. Congressman Vince Fong, R-California, led the bill in the House, which passed it earlier this year. “I’m grateful to President Trump for signing the Clergy Act into law today and for standing with the faith leaders who serve our communities daily. Pastors, priests, and ministers are pillars of their communities for a reason, and they deserve the chance to build a secure retirement for themselves and their families. Many made this decision at the very start of their ministry without fully understanding what it would mean down the road, and I’m thrilled they will now have the chance to re-enroll in these important benefits.

I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. **I’m rooted in faith, built on family, and committed to making Alabama stronger and better for generations to come.** Alabama is a place of hard work, strong values, and unyielding independence. But the Left is trying to tear that all down. I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for every Alabamian who feels forgotten and left behind. Whether it’s securing our borders, protecting our children, or defending our way of life, I’m here fighting for Alabama’s future. **This fight isn’t easy, but it's worth it. And I’m not going anywhere.** Will you stand with me?

clean_body: | | | | | | | The United States Army’s announcement on Tuesday that Fort Rucker will serve as its Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) Autonomy Center of Excellence marks a major milestone for our military, for Enterprise, and for southeast Alabama. This new designation is a recognition of Fort Rucker’s role in the future of Army Aviation and an opportunity for our region to be part of the development, training, and innovation that will help shape that future. The effort was spearheaded by Enterprise native Katie Britt, who started this project when she served as Chief of Staff to Sen. Richard Shelby and finished it as the U.S. Senator for Alabama with Tuesday’s announcement. | | U.S. Senator Katie Britt, R-Alabama, on Tuesday celebrated President Donald Trump’s signing of the Clergy Act, legislation she ushered unanimously through the Senate alongside Senator Maggie Hassan, D-New Hampshire, earlier this month. Congressman Vince Fong, R-California, led the bill in the House, which passed it earlier this year. “I’m grateful to President Trump for signing the Clergy Act into law today and for standing with the faith leaders who serve our communities daily. Pastors, priests, and ministers are pillars of their communities for a reason, and they deserve the chance to build a secure retirement for themselves and their families. Many made this decision at the very start of their ministry without fully understanding what it would mean down the road, and I’m thrilled they will now have the chance to re-enroll in these important benefits. | | | | | | | | I didn’t run for Senate to sit on the sidelines. I’m a mom, a conservative, and proud to stand for every corner of Alabama—our cities, small towns, and rural communities alike. I’m rooted in faith, built on family, and committed to making Alabama stronger and better for generations to come. Alabama is a place of hard work, strong values, and unyielding independence. But the Left is trying to tear that all down. I didn’t come to Washington to play games. I came to fight for every Alabamian who feels forgotten and left behind. Peter, As I write this, rumors are swirling that the United States is about to launch a fresh wave of strikes on Iran, with reporting from allies in the region that they've been alerted ahead of the impending action. Before the bombs start falling again, we need to look back at what this war has already cost us. And the ledger is missing a lot of data the American people deserve to know. Today's update makes it five straight weeks of writing to you because this administration got caught lying about the devastation of Trump's illegal war in Iran. **This week our justifiably fed-up troops started talking.** Troops and military families just handed _VoteVets_ and _MeidasTouch_ dozens of photos the Pentagon never wanted you to see. Burned aircraft on the tarmac. Bombed-out barracks and dining halls. Our service members in the UAE found out their own war had started by watching the news. Their protection plan amounted to digging their own foxholes.
